items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without waiting for a patch or restart. In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service while the system continued operating. The project combines OpenAI's frontier AI, security, and infrastructure research with Cisco's infrastructure and security expertise to help teams navigate the tradeoff between blocking an exploitable operation—which could take a service offline—and allowing legitimate requests through. Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system, enabling observation of suspicious activity and application of targeted protections. The company describes four core capabilities: live protection, which lets shields block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system while teams monitor how proposed shields affect applications before enforcing them; defense at machine speed, giving agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads with security teams controlling deployment; trusted deployment, where shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading using Linux's eBPF verifier and kernel security controls; and hardware-backed verification via a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) that supports a verifiable record of protections being loaded or removed. OpenAI and Cisco state they will open-source Shirudo so developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators can inspect the code, test protections, and contribute to its development.
items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Launch Shirudo Runtime for Live Linux Protection

items.summary:
Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, just days after the board had rejected his offer to return and less than two weeks after he resigned over reports of an affair with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. The company said it received input from senior US government levels and concluded that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.

The move came under pressure from President Donald Trump, who on Monday claimed he "made the deal" to convince Nvidia's board to reverse course. In a CNBC interview, Trump said he had spoken with the board of directors and "convinced" them to bring Huang back, praising their decision as responsible while noting they sought assurance about national security threats.

The reinstatement ended a week-long losing streak in US stocks that had pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory. Nvidia's stock fell sharply after Huang stepped down but jumped by 31% on Monday following his reappointment, adding approximately $1tn to the company's market value; its closing price remained slightly below Friday morning's opening level.

Board Chairman Harvey C Jones stated in a statement that "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers." Huang had resigned on 12 November following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang. On Monday, the US Commerce Department announced it was preparing to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia customer where Alice Huang served as CEO.

The reinstatement drew criticism from lawmakers across party lines. Prof Stuart Russell, a UC Berkeley computer science professor and head of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI, told the BBC that the board faced "enormous pressure" from the White House and suggested the administration worried markets would fall further without Huang's return.

Republican congressman Don Bacon said Nvidia should have moved on without Huang rather than yield to what he called an "inexplicable desire to save Huang," warning against giving China access to US technology. Sen Tom Cotton vowed Congress would investigate, calling the Megaspeed controversy merely "the tip of the iceberg." Democrats who will control both chambers from January also promised investigations; Senator Elizabeth Warren, set to chair the Senate Banking Committee, called the reinstatement "reckless," while Rep Sydney Kamlager-Dove condemned it as "premature" before investigations conclude. Rep Andre Carson said Congress needs a full accounting of whether controlled technology was diverted to China.

Huang is scheduled for a closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December, followed by testimony before the Senate banking committee two days later.

Trump has accumulated significant Nvidia investments since returning to the White House. Financial disclosures show he purchased $265,000 in stock and sold as much as $15,000 worth of shares in September. A BBC review indicates purchases ranging between $23m and $86m (£18m and £66m), with 85 separate transactions across multiple accounts over two years. Trump also made gains from 19 sales totaling between $3.5m and $10.2m, though the value of his holdings would have been affected by Nvidia's stock decline during Huang's exit.

Both Trump and the White House rejected claims that he profited from the presidency; Trump said "everybody" was making money from rising stocks and does not make decisions related to his investment accounts, while noting his businesses are held in a trust managed by his sons.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang After Affair and National Security Concerns

On Tuesday (Nov. 24), Asian shares surged following a Wall Street rally triggered by Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia CEO, which revived the battered AI trade while Federal Reserve tightening bets lifted Treasury yields and the dollar. MSCI's broadest Asia-Pacific index outside Japan climbed 4.6 percent to its biggest single-day gain in two weeks after an eight-month low; Japan's Nikkei added 4.5 percent (aided by traders returning from a local holiday), South Korea's KOSPI jumped 7.5 percent, and Taiwan's shares rose 9.1 percent.

Huang's return followed Nvidia's Monday gain of 31.5 percent—the company's biggest daily percentage increase in 23 years—restoring nearly $1 trillion in value, while the Nasdaq 100 jumped more than 6 percent as AI-industry shares rallied broadly. Capital.com senior financial market analyst Kyle Rodda said Huang's return eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade at least marginally, though concerns over slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth persist; he also flagged upcoming Wednesday PCE Index data ahead of the Fed's final 2026 meeting as a risk.

The rebound revived bets on near-term Federal Reserve tightening: CME Group's FedWatch tool shows traders now price a December rate hike as certain (up from 89 percent odds Friday), with roughly a 5 percent chance of a 50-basis-point increase. The benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.94 percent and the 2-year note climbed to 4.69 percent, while the dollar hovered near a more than 19-month high against the euro.

In commodities, oil fell more than 3 percent toward a three-month low on rising Middle East supplies that offset shipping and refinery attack worries; Brent crude settled flat at $89.50 per barrel after Monday's drop to $89.37. Spot gold recovered from a one-year low, finishing up 0.7 percent at $3,657.97 per ounce as investors bought the dip.
items.title: Asian Stocks Rally as Jensen Huang's Return Revives AI Trade

items.summary: The US Department of Commerce announced it intends to add Singapore-based data center developer Megaspeed Ltd to a blacklist barring the company from buying or selling goods in America, though no effective date was specified. The move follows allegations that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang worked as an intelligence asset for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, raising concerns about whether Megaspeed funneled advanced AI chips into China. US officials had been investigating the company for nearly two years and suspected it violated export controls by helping route Nvidia's restricted chips to Chinese firms; Alibaba has reportedly been one of its largest customers through subsidiary Speedmatrix, which was also added to the blacklist. China denied Huang is a spy and warned against using the scandal as a pretext for an AI technology blockade. The ban comes amid ongoing fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation on November 12 over separate affair allegations, after which Nvidia's board reinstated him following intervention by President Donald Trump; both his departure and return caused Nvidia's stock to fall more than 30% before rallying again. Huang and Nvidia's chief legal officer are set to appear at a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee as multiple government agency investigations continue.

items.summary: US stocks soared on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive following pressure from President Donald Trump, sparking a sharp reversal of last week's global equity market rout that had been triggered in part by the chipmaker's leadership crisis. Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% before closing 31% higher, driving a broad rally across technology stocks on Wall Street. The Nasdaq 100 rose 6.5%, the S&P 500 added 4.7%, and Europe's STOXX 600 gained 1.8%. Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, said he does not believe the rebound has run its course and that it is not too late to gradually add back technology exposure. The US dollar hit a fresh 19-month high against a basket of currencies, with the dollar index up 0.45% at 104.31. Huang's brief absence had roiled markets already concerned about AI investment valuations; Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot in London, said his departure poured petrol on an already volatile AI trade and that his return should help take some heat out of the market. Huang resigned following reports of several extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect of being a spy for China, which he has not directly addressed. Nvidia's board had last week ruled out a return for Huang, but Trump pushed for reinstatement and said his return poses no risk to US national security—a statement numerous lawmakers questioned on Monday. Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its biggest decline since the March 2020 pandemic-driven selloff, while Wall Street's fear gauge rose above 40 for the first time since April 2025. The fall in Taiwan's chipmaker-heavy benchmark last week was the biggest since 1990, and European shares posted their worst weekly performance in almost eight months. In Asia's Monday session, Taiwan stocks rose 2.1% with government support helping to stabilize the market, while South Korea's KOSPI came off 10-month lows to trade down 3.3%. The US-listed iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF rose nearly 18%, surging following news of Huang's return. South Korea's finance minister reiterated plans to stabilize the market if necessary, and Taiwan's financial regulator ordered a tightening of short-selling rules while China announced support measures such as easing margin financing requirements. Safe-haven buying of US bonds reversed after Friday's surge: the yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes added around 2.37 basis points to 4.94%, and the 2-year note rose 7.44 basis points to 4.69%. Gold extended gains to trade up 2.9% at $3,661 an ounce while Bitcoin rose less than 1%; oil fell as increased Middle East supplies offset unease about shipping and refinery attacks in the region, with Brent closing down 3.5% at $89.34 a barrel.

items.summary:
An Iran-based foreign influence operation used AI-generated personas, including a fake journalist named Alice Johnson, to produce news articles and social media posts about Australia's involvement in the US-Iran War. The ABC reports that OpenAI disclosed last month it detected and disrupted this campaign, which it dubbed "Bogus Bylines." According to OpenAI's report, actors used several ChatGPT accounts from Iran to create personas for seven fake Western journalists who pitched nearly 100 articles to online publications and posted on social media. The report did not note that at least one persona, Alice Johnson, repeatedly wrote about Australian politics.

The ABC can reveal new details showing the campaign targeted Australia throughout. Web pages and posts attributed to Johnson but since removed show she published at least two articles mentioning Australia. Her first article appeared in Middle East Monitor in March, arguing Australia's lack of immediate plans to send navy ships to the Strait of Hormuz signaled division among US allies; Semrush estimated that publication received about 22,000 Australian visits in October and posted it on a Facebook page with more than 2 million followers. In another outlet, Geopolitical Monitor, Johnson used cuts to Australia's fuel excise as evidence Western countries were bearing the conflict's costs.

On X (formerly Twitter), the now-suspended @ImAliceJohnson account posted more than 100 times, including several references to Australia. It shared videos of a Sydney protest against Israeli President Isaac Herzog's visit and re-shared footage of former Australian of the Year Grace Tame with commentary about Israel's image "collapsing under truth." The account also repeatedly engaged an Australian academic and other users.

OpenAI said its report found that while the operation's social media presence likely had little impact, publishing to multiple outlets with significant audiences gave it a notable effect. A separate Meta report earlier this year identified @ImAliceJohnson as part of an Iran-based influence network dating back to 2024.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong will raise the AI-fuelled operation in Parliament today as an example of foreign actors using new technology for ill, relying on OpenAI's disclosure. QUT digital influence researcher Dr Timothy Graham said state-based actors use such technology to destabilize and cause division by targeting wedge issues rather than persuading people toward a single political objective; he cautioned that the accounts' views should be seen as tactics to sow discord in the attention economy, not honest endorsements.

RMIT lecturer Gordon Farrer suggested one campaign objective may be to influence AI itself, noting published articles get reincorporated into AI training. OpenAI has yet to respond to a request for comment.
items.title: Iran-Based Operation Used ChatGPT to Create Fake Journalist Targeting Australia

items.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department added Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, along with six other companies from Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, to its Entity List on Monday over alleged diversion of artificial intelligence chips to China, intensifying scrutiny surrounding the Nvidia controversy. As an Nvidia partner, Megaspeed has been under investigation by U.S. authorities since 2024 amid allegations that it diverted AI chips to China; placement on the list means these companies will require Commerce Department approval for American exports, with such requests likely denied, Reuters reported. The action followed criticism from lawmakers and administration officials over the delay in blacklisting Megaspeed, prompting Senator Pete Ricketts of Nebraska to post on X that "the department of commerce still needs to explain to Commerce why this took so long," while a Commerce Department official said the six other companies added also had links to Megaspeed. The move came after reports emerged earlier this month about an alleged affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed; U.S. authorities suspect Alice Huang of being a Chinese spy, though China has dismissed those allegations as "groundless." Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had criticized the Commerce Department for not placing Megaspeed on the Entity List earlier and questioned whether Nvidia adequately monitored its customers and chip sales. In response to the controversy, Nvidia said it recently formed an export control committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks, stated that it conducts legitimate and lawful business while complying with U.S. export controls, and noted that Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed in August 2025. Separately, a joint statement from the Justice Department and Commerce Department last week said they would "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred," while Democratic lawmakers opened a probe into whether Nvidia exerted influence over the Commerce Department's investigation. The blacklisting arrives as Huang has returned as Nvidia CEO after stepping down two weeks ago amid reports about his alleged relationships, including an extramarital affair with Alice Huang.
items.title: US Blacklists Megaspeed Amid Nvidia Chip Diversion Probe

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has proposed new safeguards against digital payment fraud as part of the draft (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026. The proposals include a 'Trusted Person Mechanism' under which account holders can voluntarily designate someone to provide an additional authentication layer for fund transfers; once activated, any transfer triggers an alert giving the trusted person one hour to approve or reject it, with unapproved transactions automatically cancelled and no financial liability placed on that person. The mechanism covers physical and digital transfers above a specified threshold but excludes UPI payments, merchant payments, and existing recurring mandates. A second measure is an account-wide 'stop switch,' available through branches, ATMs, net banking, mobile apps, and IVR, which lets customers block outgoing payments, new mandates, and third-party app UPI registration immediately if they suspect their account has been compromised; incoming credits, existing recurring mandates, and bank-initiated recoveries would continue. An earlier proposal of one-hour latency for transfers has been dropped, while deactivation requires stringent authentication and a risk-based cooling period. Customers can also switch digital channels on or off, set disabling time windows and transaction limits by channel, beneficiary, or day, and debit, credit, and prepaid cards will have similar controls across domestic/international, ATM, PoS, online, and contactless transactions—excluding gift and transit PPIs—with new accounts having digital channels disabled by default for the first 24 hours after activation. New cards would initially permit only domestic contact-based ATM and PoS transactions. The framework also expands bank negligence to cover failures in multi-factor authentication, customer-set controls, fraud alerts, 24x7 reporting, prompt action on complaints, failure to block channels after repeated failed logins, system malfunctions, bank-side security breaches, and collusion by employees or vendors. These rules apply to commercial banks but exclude small finance banks, payments banks, RRBs, and local area banks.
items.title: RBI Proposes Trusted Approver and Stop Switch to Curb Digital Payment Fraud

Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive who resigned earlier this month amid allegations of multiple extramarital affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy, returned to the role after an 11-day absence. According to a statement from Nvidia's board citing 'input from senior levels of the United States government,' President Donald Trump reportedly appeared at the board meeting and lobbied for Huang's reinstatement; Trump later told CNBC he 'spoke to them' and 'convinced them.' In a video message posted to social media, Huang thanked employees for giving him 'a second chance' and said he would be 'a better CEO the second time around,' addressing cheering Nvidia workers. The board chair, Harvey C. Jones, had used the company's recent quarterly earnings call — during which Nvidia reported better-than-expected results and raised its sales guidance — to signal that it did not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO following findings that his behavior was 'inconsistent with its code of conduct.'

Huang's return produced a sharp rally in Nvidia shares, though several power and grid companies also saw their stocks rise. Constellation, part of an Nvidia collaboration developing AI factories designed as flexible energy assets for faster grid connection, increased 6%. GE Vernova, which uses Nvidia's AI factory reference design to unlock grid capacity, rallied more than 8%. Bloom Energy, which has no direct Nvidia relationship but markets fuel cells aligned with Nvidia's chip roadmap, rose more than 18%.

Peter Hans Hirschboeck, founder and managing director of impactECI Energy (an advisor to Emerald AI), said the market-wide reaction reflected investor reluctance to have a 'ruddless ship' at a company with outsized influence on both the AI industry and the U.S. economy; he noted that investors felt they needed Huang back despite the scandal, though Hirschboeck declined direct comment on Emerald AI's partnership given his advisory role.

The reaction contrasted sharply with criticism from Congressional Democrats. Sen. Chuck Schumer called for an investigation into 'any wrongdoing by the Trump administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.' Sen. Chris Van Hollen posted that 'This is what a rigged system looks like,' alleging Trump traded Nvidia stock while the company donated $25 million to his ballroom before securing Huang's return.

Additional scrutiny continues: Nvidia executives are scheduled to appear before Congressional committees early next month, and on Friday the New York Times reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices. Hirschboeck characterized the situation as one of ongoing volatility, noting it has 'become normal to hear a breaking piece of market-moving news every 6 hours.'

items.summary: In the New South Wales Supreme Court, barrister John Stratton SC concluded his closing statement on Tuesday morning by telling a jury that his client, Beau Lamarre-Condon, voluntarily chose to testify rather than remain silent. Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his partner Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird's Paddington home on 19 February 2024, having pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter. Stratton said Lamarre-Condon could have told the crown 'do your worst but I'm not going to help you,' but instead took what he called a 'long walk' to the witness box and subjected himself to cross-examination by an experienced crown prosecutor that lasted over six days, arguing it did not break down his client or establish new lies. Stratton emphasized that giving evidence does not require Lamarre-Condon to prove his case, noting the onus of proof remains with the crown throughout. The double murder trial is expected to conclude in the coming days as the jury prepares for deliberations, and Justice Natalie Adams will spend the afternoon instructing the jurors.
items.title: Barrister Says Beau Lamarre-Condon Chose Witness Box Over Silence in Double Murder Trial

items.summary: Databricks announced support for catalog labels through a new capability called Tag Exchange, which exposes Unity Catalog's table- and column-level tags through the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API. The feature is available in Beta today, with users able to enable it by activating 'Tag Exchange via Iceberg REST Catalog' in the Databricks Previews portal. To implement catalog labels, Databricks worked with the Apache Iceberg community to add an optional labels field to the Iceberg REST LoadTable response, providing catalogs a standard way to expose table- and column-level context such as business ownership, intended use, sensitivity, and other metadata. Catalog labels are string key-value pairs that share this context through the API without prescribing its vocabulary or interpretation, allowing each platform flexibility in how it builds on them while retaining its own capabilities and controls. The announcement is supported by Google Cloud, Salesforce, ClickHouse, Atlan, Collibra, DataHub, Immuta, Trust3 AI, PhoenixAI, and Datastrato, which joined Databricks to advance the shared vision of metadata interoperability across open lakehouse architectures. Gaurav Saxena, Director of Product Management at Google Cloud, stated that catalog labels are taking shape in the Apache Iceberg community as an open protocol for exchanging live governance tags across catalogs and engines, complementing Open Knowledge Format (OKF) as a higher-level standard for portable business semantics. The article illustrates how these labels work with a table named support_cases: an authorized data steward assigns domain=customer_support and system.certification_status=certified to the table along with content_type=support_case_summary to the issue_summary column, which a catalog can expose in its LoadTable response so downstream platforms can use them. PyIceberg has added support for accessing catalog labels in Python, with applications able to inspect these labels starting in the next 0.13 release. Don Bosco Durai, CTO of Trust3 AI, noted that classification is only useful if it reaches where access decisions are made, and Tag Exchange enables a sensitivity label set once in Unity Catalog to drive policy in platforms like Trust3 AI without a separate metadata project. Chandru Sugunan, Director of Product at Atlan, described a company's context as its intellectual property that should be portable across every platform. Narinder Singh, VP of Product Management at Salesforce, expressed excitement about working with Databricks and the broader ecosystem to enable metadata sharing so AI agents can operate with consistent business semantics.
items.title: Databricks Adds Tag Exchange to Expose Unity Catalog Labels via Apache Iceberg REST

items.summary: This report is the first installment of a series analyzing the software supply chain threat landscape. It examined approximately 5,400 confirmed malicious npm packages published between December 2025 and October 2026—the first year following npm's revocation of long-lived authentication tokens on December 9, 2025 [1]. Packages were detected by the authors' scanner analyzing npm publish events for suspicious activity, then filtered to retain only those with at least one independent source: a public advisory, a vendor-published campaign report, an npm security takedown, or analyst review. Time is measured by npm publish date; the unit of record is package version (dated by first malicious version); and download counts are monthly snapshots recorded at scan time.
items.title: Analysis of ~5,400 Confirmed Malicious npm Packages in the Year After Long-Lived Token Revocation

visual.alt: Bar chart. August 2026 (single dependency-confusion campaign) 78 %; March 2026 (npm token theft peak) 22 %; May–October 2026 (other months) 5 %.

items.summary: The Trump administration left open the prospect of Jensen Huang returning to lead Nvidia even as scrutiny over his resignation intensified, according to reporting. President Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made remarks suggesting this openness, standing in contrast to growing hawkishness from Washington officials about the episode. A right-leaning Washington Post columnist warned that US AI policy had "a chip-size hole in it" and argued for stricter enforcement of export controls. Huang was forced out as CEO over his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, a situation driving anger over Nvidia's role in supplying chips to China. The prospect of tighter curbs has already impacted the AI supply chain in Asia, per Nikkei reporting.
items.title: Trump Administration Leaves Door Open for Jensen Huang's Nvidia Return

items.summary: According to the 2026 Asia Power Index released by Lowy Institute, Prime Minister Narendra Modi climbed three places to rank as Asia's second-most effective leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping. The index rated India's 'diplomatic influence' as its strongest measure, with an expert survey rating Modi more highly for his effectiveness in advancing India's diplomatic interests in Asia than in prior assessments. This improvement came despite a relatively subdued Indian diplomatic profile during the Gulf conflict, which the report said weighed on perceptions of his global leadership and strategic ambition. The 2026 findings point to a more prominent Indian role in an increasingly competitive Asian strategic landscape, even as the US and China continue to dominate the regional power structure. India's gains have been driven by diplomatic engagement, regional security cooperation, investment attractiveness, cultural influence, demographic prospects, and its ability to maintain economic relationships during weakening regional conditions. Separately, India's membership in tracked diplomatic forums rose two places to a joint second position; it was represented in 17 of the summits, clubs, and inter-governmental organizations Lowy tracks, level with Indonesia and Thailand and one behind China.
items.title: Modi Ranks as Asia's Second-Most Effective Leader After Xi in 2026 Index

items.summary: On Monday, a Supreme Court bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana chastised an additional sessions judge in Sasaram, Bihar, over his handling of a criminal case against a superintendent of police (SP). The judicial officer had directed the SP to file an FIR against a witness for allegedly deposing falsely. After repeated summons went unfulfilled, he asked the Bihar chief secretary to take disciplinary action; when that failed, he registered a criminal case and ordered the SP's appearance on August 22. Following two adjournments—during which the SP's counsel sought permission for a virtual appearance citing flood relief duties—the inspecting judge from the High Court requested that the sessions judge meet him with case records in Patna on September 24, an invitation the judicial officer declined, describing it as "very humiliating and demoralising." On September 29, he convicted the SP of flouting court orders and imposed a fine of Re 1. The state government appealed to the Patna High Court, which criticised the judge's conduct and urged him to be circumspect in future proceedings. Hurt by these remarks, the judicial officer approached the Supreme Court, arguing that "the present case depicts the pitiable plight of judicial officers once they pass any order against an IAS or IPS officer," contending that the system tends to protect such officials while leaving judges unsupported. The bench questioned whether a district judge could behave in this manner and asked why he would not comply with the inspecting judge's request, stating that "every judge must know the contours of his jurisdiction." It further instructed counsel Prem Prakash to convey to the judicial officer that he should not become "Baahubali of Bihar," warning him against being Quixotic or playing Robin Hood. The bench also requested the High Court to consider the petitioner's explanation-cum-apology sympathetically and dispose of pending proceedings, despite observations made in its October 8 order. In a separate matter involving another judicial officer petitioning over promotion and selection for higher judicial service, the CJI-led bench observed that it has become customary for such officers to approach the Supreme Court directly without first consulting the concerned High Courts, noting they focus excessively on promotions, salary increases, perks, and retirement age extensions while paying little attention to addressing case pendency.
items.title: Supreme Court Reprimands Bihar Judge for Registering Criminal Case Against SP

items.summary: Francesco Bianchi, Era Dabla-Norris, Radhika Goyal, Victoria Haver, and Salma Khalid study how individuals form expectations about fiscal adjustment in their NBER Working Paper 36043 (2026). Using survey data from more than 27,000 respondents across 13 countries, the authors jointly elicit beliefs about current fiscal conditions, expectations of tax increases and spending cuts, and open-ended explanations for those expectations. They classify these explanations into economic mental models, political narratives, and experience-based heuristics.
items.title: Mental Models of Fiscal Policy

items.title: Jacobs and Layton Estimate Medicare Advantage Enrollment Elasticity to Private Plan Subsidies

items.summary: Asia Pacific has experienced strong economic growth over recent decades, but its momentum could be slowed by two demographic and disease trends: rapidly ageing populations and a growing chronic disease burden. Several economies are becoming 'super-ageing' societies with more than 20 per cent of the population aged 65 or older, while major non-communicable diseases account for nearly nine in 10 deaths in the Western Pacific and more than half of all deaths in Southeast Asia; around one in three adults in Asia live with two or more long-term conditions. Ill health can prevent people from working independently or caring for loved ones, and a Marsh & McLennan report estimated it could cost regional countries between 9 per cent and 12 per cent of GDP.
items.title: Why better health is an investment in Asia-Pacific's future

items.summary: Green Party leader Zack Polanski has endorsed a report from the Verdant thinktank that calls for Britain to remain in NATO and maintain its nuclear weapons, according to party sources. The Green Party says its defence policies have not changed since 2024, when it campaigned on signing the UN treaty banning nuclear weapons and dismantling Trident submarines immediately; however, party officials described Polanski's endorsement as part of an internal debate about reassuring voters on national security issues. In a statement, Polanski said: “At its core, national security is about food on the table, warm homes and safe communities. That makes it a progressive issue – and I welcome Verdant’s call for a comprehensive security framework that brings people from across the UK into keeping our country safe.” Report author Sacha Deshmukh added: “Historically some progressives have shied away from recognising security threats. But the right has not been willing to accept the flaws in their policy solutions, so they are not always as strong as they should be – both sides need to change that.” A YouGov poll last year showed just 17% of voters trusted the Greens on defence — the lowest trust rating across 18 different issues. Concerns about Green positions on defence have led some members to call for ending opposition to drones and anti-ballistic missiles, causing an internal rift ahead of this year's conference; the Verdant report is expected to trigger further debate within the party given its close links to the Greens despite being independent. The report recommends that the government rethink national security strategy toward value for money — such as buying off-the-shelf weapons rather than designing bespoke systems — and increase investment in climate adaptation, which some in the green movement view sceptically as diverting attention from preventing climate deterioration. On NATO, Deshmukh calls for UK membership while pushing for reform of alliance structures alongside allies; this mirrors official Green Party policy but contradicts Polanski's earlier personal statement on the Guardian's Politics Weekly podcast that Trump’s dominance within NATO makes internal reform impossible. Regarding the nuclear deterrent, Deshmukh argues the UK could not and potentially should not cancel the Dreadnought submarine contract, while also advocating closer cooperation with France on missiles being developed to carry US Trident warheads — a position he noted is currently under development. Any commitment to the nuclear deterrent would contrast sharply with the Greens' pre-election promise that elected members would push for immediate dismantling of UK nuclear weapons.
items.title: Zack Polanski backs Verdant report endorsing Nato membership and nuclear weapons

items.summary: A Southern Natural Gas Company pipeline exploded Saturday night in rural Sumter County, Alabama, about eight miles east of the Mississippi state line near Ward. The fireball leaped hundreds of feet into the air at approximately 11:27 p.m., was visible from more than 50 miles away and on weather radar according to local meteorologists, and caused no reported injuries per the company and local officials. Mayor Renee Ward Pringle of nearby York (population 2,400) said residents were asking about the flames but that preliminary information is encouraging without premature safety assurances. Southern Natural Gas Company is jointly owned by Kinder Morgan and Southern Company and operated by Kinder Morgan; it runs roughly 7,000 miles of pipelines distributing fossil gas throughout the Southeast to major gas-fired power plants run by Southern Company subsidiaries including Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power. Kinder Morgan described the blast as a force majeure incident—a natural gas release and fire on a pipeline segment—with no further cause released as of Monday afternoon; the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration confirmed staff were deployed and its investigation is ongoing. Portia Shepherd, executive director of Blackbelt Women Rising, called it a warning shot, saying such explosions recur while SNG plans to expand via South System Expansion 4 (SSE4), which would increase pipeline capacity by about 1.3 billion cubic feet per day—enough methane to fill nearly 15,000 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Federal regulators issued orders forcing corrective actions after explosions along other sections of the pipeline in 2022 and 2026. In October, attorneys for the Southern Environmental Law Center filed a lawsuit on behalf of impacted landowners and nine nonprofits across the South—including Shepherd's—to set aside a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ruling authorizing SSE4 across Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia; SELC attorney Megan Gibson called Saturday's explosion a stark reminder that risks to communities along these routes are real. The Alabama Rivers Alliance warned that federal permitting legislation (the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act) would fast-track pipelines like this one and put more Alabama communities in danger. Shepherd said residents lack comprehensive safety plans for such incidents, questioned where visible safety measures are, and expressed distrust of Kinder Morgan's motives.
items.title: Alabama Pipeline Explosion and Fight Over Expansion

items.summary:
A custody dispute over a popular tabby cat named Parhan at Senayan City shopping centre in Jakarta has been resolved. The friendly community cat, nicknamed the "handsome one" and "celebrity of Senayan," disappeared from the mall overnight in October after a woman named Citra Putri posted on Threads that she intended to adopt him and take him to Sydney between her homes in Tangerang and Sydney. A security guard had found Parhan nearby in August, where he became cared for by everyone at the mall but owned by no one. The disappearance triggered an uproar covered by major Indonesian media outlets including Kompas, Detik, and CNN Indonesia; social media analyst Syifa Nabila Syaharani Jauhari told the ABC that on some days Parhan received more mentions on X than former vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation on November 12. Lawyer Winda Yunika offered pro bono help to reclaim Parhan, telling the ABC another security guard had seen a woman with a cat carrier when he disappeared.

The intense public attention prompted Jakarta government officials to facilitate a meeting attended by Ms Putri, animal welfare advocates, and Senayan City management. Spokesperson Chico Hakim said the provincial government stepped in following calls from members of the public and animal welfare communities regarding the removal of Parhan, aiming for resolution with the animal's welfare as top priority. In a video posted online, Ms Putri apologised "for all of the commotion that has happened," saying she was wrong because she only found out later that Parhan already had people caring for him.

All parties agreed in a mediation document viewed by the ABC that Parhan would be returned to Senayan City. His legal representative returned him on November 18 after they said he needed treatment for a medical issue, with Jakarta provincial parliament member Francine Widjojo addressing journalists as the cat climbed onto her back and described him as startled while readjusting. Ms Yunika noted that Parhan appeared traumatised by the experience, preferring to hide in bushes when seeing people looking for him, and said his case served as an example that anyone wishing to adopt a cat should go through proper procedures rather than adopting cats that have already gone viral.
items.title: Jakarta Government Mediates Resolution in Viral Custody Dispute Over 'Handsome' Cat Parhan

items.summary: Indian Railways has excluded the Tatkal quota from its new premium overnight service, the Vande Bharat Sleeper, making berths available under the general reservation quota and eliminating RAC tickets. The move comes amid a financial backdrop in which passenger operations posted an operating loss of ₹63,721 crore in FY25 while freight services generated an operating profit of ₹50,505 crore, reflecting decades-old cross-subsidisation that uses goods profits to cover carrying losses. Although Tatkal tickets bring extra revenue and premium overnight trains seem like a natural place for higher fares, the decision echoes Railways' earlier dynamic-pricing experiment: Flexi-Fare launched in September 2016 on Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto trains increased fares as seats filled but drew criticism from a 2018 Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit. The CAG found that Flexi-Fare raised vacant berths in AC 3-tier from 0.66% to 4.46% and cut passengers on affected premium trains by 6.75 lakh, while fares sometimes exceeded flights on overlapping routes without guaranteeing a confirmed berth for waitlisted tickets; following feedback the Ministry of Railways withdrew Flexi-Fare from 15 low-occupancy trains (below 50% average monthly occupancy) and cut maximum fare multipliers with discounts up to 20%. For Vande Bharat Sleeper, which has 823 berths concentrated in AC 3-tier — a class that posted an operational surplus of ₹3,645 crore in FY25 versus a ₹19,158 crore loss for Slepper Class per the CAG's 2026 report — keeping fares predictable and occupancy high may be more profitable than extracting premiums from last-minute bookers. The article also points to revenue diversification models abroad: Japan Railway East (JR East), where transportation made up roughly 67% of consolidated operating revenue in FY25 with retail, services, real estate and hotels contributing the remaining 33%, and Hong Kong's MTR 'Rail Plus Property' model that captures land-value uplift around stations. The piece concludes that railways may earn more by keeping fares predictable, filling berths, and pursuing unconventional revenue sources rather than simply charging passengers higher fares.
items.title: Indian Railways Abandons Tatkal on Vande Bharat Sleeper Trains

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for a new round of four-way negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia, the United States, and European leaders to be held as soon as possible. Speaking by video to NATO lawmakers in Berlin, he said Kyiv is ready to meet 'literally tomorrow,' noting that partners have indicated they want to try to hold talks before Christmas while hoping for something sooner. Zelensky welcomed the latest push for peace discussions with Moscow and added a repeated plea for Ukraine's full membership in NATO rather than only receiving security guarantees from alliance countries, arguing that his country's combat experience, defense industry, and large military would strengthen the alliance. European governments have been excluded from past negotiations, and their push to join talks has gained prominence recently. Zelensky acknowledged that some NATO leaders remain hesitant about admitting Ukraine; NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said after Zelensky that joining requires unanimous support but rejected any idea that Russia could dictate membership decisions. Separately, US envoy Jared Kushner had told Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week that Washington might consider offering a security guarantee similar to Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement. In response, Zelensky said major questions remain about how such guarantees would function without full NATO commitment, asking which countries would support Ukraine if attacked again, what partners would do, which troops would be stationed in advance, and how much it would cost, adding that clear specific answers had not been heard so far. He also called on NATO countries to provide more air defense weapons, urging them to empty their stockpiles so Ukraine can repel Russian airstrikes.
items.title: Zelensky Urges Four-Way Peace Talks with Russia, Europe and US 'As Soon as Possible'

items.summary: Chinese AI lab Z.ai released GLM-5.4 on November 23, 2026, marking its first use of a looped transformer architecture in which a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations to refine hidden states from the previous pass, yielding deeper networks without increasing parameter count. The model is not yet available as open weights; it can only be accessed via Z.ai's Coding Plan subscription API key on their OpenAI-compatible Responses API endpoint, and the author built an llm-glm plugin because existing plugins like llm-zai did not yet support 5.4. GLM-5.4 follows Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini (November 20), which runs its middle layers three times per token to improve reasoning on agentic coding tasks with fewer tokens.
items.title: Z.ai Releases GLM-5.4 With Its First Loop Transformer Architecture

items.summary: In an interview with Scroll, Jawaharlal Nehru University professor Ghazala Jamil discussed her new book, What to Do with Political Sadness, in which she argues that sadness can be political and stems from the loss of a future that once seemed within grasp but no longer feels tenable. Jamil traced the concept's origins to Mark Fisher's hauntology, describing how futures that never came to be continue to haunt society; however, her book locates hauntology in the Indian context to examine state violence, citizen protests, and notions of belonging. She explained that for Indians who grew up in the 1980s and 1990s, the 21st century seemed full of promise—Rajiv Gandhi made 'the 21st Century' a political slogan tied to technological advancement—and argued that these lost futures demand honest mourning because being pushed into forgetting them wounds and festers. Jamil said what haunts her is believing she raised children in an India more secular than the one they now inhabit, noting Indians lack language for this disappointment and stuckness. She contended that for marginalised minorities, the distinction between public and private feelings blurs because personal feelings result from public issues; citing the demolition of the Babri Masjid as a symbolic wound and explaining that when there is no public redressal, political wounding gets internalised while insisting on justice risks being branded communal. On dominant groups' political grief, she said she takes seriously Hindus who support the Ram Janmabhoomi movement speaking of a '500-year struggle,' arguing everyone's sense of community and history is curated and that victim narratives are legitimising even when lacking evidence; she added that more information does not automatically make people rational because these narratives are experienced viscerally, noting Hindu cultural nationalists' opposition to Muslim 'foreignness' was in tandem with British colonialism. When asked why her book gives the impression of obsession with death, Jamil said as a Muslim she is always reminded of death and raised mindful of mortality from childhood; she described being moved by Tamil Nadu farmers who protested at Jantar Mantar using novel forms of protest that grew more abject each day, saying state violence and citizens' powerlessness when targeted have long occupied her mind. Regarding the Assamese musician Zubeen Garg's death, in which his fans were for a long time in denial, she characterised humans taking risks unwisely as on par with curiosity and stupidity while focusing on the commercialisation of this instinct among rich and powerful people who dabbled in dangerous acts historically. On Indians' reactions to Mohandas Gandhi's assassination, Jamil said narrowing discourse about Partition trauma at that time led to revival of support for Nathuram Godse; she declined to offer counterfactuals but wished those closest to Gandhi had considered what he was trying to do regarding fair opposition to Partition, arguing states tend to sanitise accounts around assassinations and people should not take their eyes off what the state is doing. On self-suffering as protest, she said fasting until death has been used when no other method exists but can also be a strategic tactic depending on what movements make of it; while Rohit Vemula did not die by suicide strategically—reaching a point where he could not go on and galvanising a movement—she described Sonam Wangchuk as really good at using the fast-during-the-Cockroach-Janta-Party-protest tactic, comparing Gandhi's meticulously planned Dandi March to protesters who played dead against the Ken-Betwa Link Project. On Rajasthan's law prohibiting corpses in protests, Jamil said death-as-protest symbolises a breakdown of the social contract between citizens and government because it conveys that the state is not preserving life but causing death through active killing or letting people die; she added that to catch attention or embarrass the state for actions in obscure places like Ken-Betwa requires performing protests media would report, ultimately making visible this breakdown. When asked why citizenship should be conferred by death too, Jamil said burial expresses belonging—'we belong here because we chose to stay here and our ancestors are buried here,' as articulated during movements against the Citizenship Amendment Act and National Register of Citizens—and pointed out that people should move freely while claiming belonging; she noted nationality was fluid only a few generations ago when people belonged to several places simultaneously, citing Maulana Azad's mixed Arab-Afghan heritage with family origins in Mecca, Delhi, and Calcutta. Finally, on moving from political sadness to hope, Jamil said that question is difficult and drew inspiration from Amitava Kumar's advice about making writing relevant rather than irrelevant; she explained being overdeterministic about what ought to be done demobilises people overwhelmed by required work, so keeping it real with frugality about individual future helps maintain hope while investing deeply in collective efforts.
items.title: Jawaharlal Nehru University Professor Ghazala Jamil on Political Sadness

items.summary:
The U.S. solar industry's flagship annual convention RE+, hosted by the Solar Energy Industries Association and the Smart Electric Power Alliance, opened last week in Las Vegas for the first time at the sprawling Las Vegas Convention Center, where Elon Musk reportedly convinced city officials to drill single-lane subterranean tubes so chauffeured Teslas could transport attendees between halls. Raghu Belur, chief products officer at Enphase, said RE+ has broadened beyond solar and batteries into a modern grid ecosystem featuring large and small batteries, grid transformers, EV chargers, data center electronics packages, and green hydrogen ventures.

The article highlights three technological innovations. First, perovskite-enhanced panels: startup Caelux prints perovskites as a thin film on standard solar glass at its Los Angeles factory and ships the glass to Heliene in Minnesota for assembly into full-size silicon-perovskite modules. Heliene advertises this panel as 27% efficient, up from its previous 24% standard, though Caelux is awaiting UL certifications before wider adoption while expanding its LA factory toward a gigafactory; global giant Qcells and startup Tandem PV have also claimed to be building the first perovskite gigafactories.

Second, shippable solar for rural America: EG4 Electronics' Homestead 60 is a pre-wired, factory-assembled 7-kilowatt solar array on a steel frame with a rugged 60-kilowatt-hour battery that functions as a microgrid. The company advertises the system at $1.20 per watt for solar only and $2.62 per watt with storage; its 14.4 kilowatt base package nearly matches EnergySage's average residential ground-mount system of nearly $3 per watt, though four racks plus a battery total $37,700.

Third, solid-state transformers: Tesla released Powercore and Drew Baglino launched Heron Power to commercialize the technology amid transformer supply chain bottlenecks; Tesla Head of Energy and Charging AJ Booth said Tesla has shipped 3 terawatts of power converters across its products. Enphase showed a prototype converting 2.5 MW using about 528 smaller boxes, with its main product twice as large. Both companies aim to begin shipping sometime next year.
items.title: RE+ Showcases Three Solar Innovations: Perovskite-Enhanced Panels, Shippable Rural Systems, and Solid-State Transformers

items.summary: IRCTC has launched a pilot project serving trimmed menus to passengers aboard three Vande Bharat sleeper trains as part of an effort to improve food quality and hygiene on long-distance rail routes. The compact menu, introduced on November 1 and modeled after airline meals, reduces the number of items served for breakfast, lunch, and dinner across the Mumbai-Bengaluru, Howrah-Kamakhya (Guwahati), and New Delhi-Varanasi Junction routes. Officials said the decision follows a verbal railway ministry direction communicated to the zones earlier this year amid frequent passenger complaints.
items.title: IRCTC Trials Smaller Menus on Long-Haul Trains in Quality Push

items.summary: At the First Kannada Comprehensive Medical Literature Conference held November 20-21, 2026 in Bengaluru, Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) administrators, linguists, and medical writers gathered to discuss introducing Kannada into medical education. The initiative coincides with a newly released three-volume Health Encyclopaedia by Dr SP Yoganna and a Kannada Medical Dictionary. RGUHS Vice-Chancellor Dr Bhagavan BC framed the move as both a communication tool for out-of-state students and a long-term academic experiment, stating that the university previously taught basic Kannada to external students so they could communicate with patients but is now exploring whether medical education itself can be taught in Kannada medium. However, ground reporting by The Federal highlights concerns about national career mobility: unlike state civil services such as KAS or IAS exams offered in regional languages, medical training in India depends on national licensing exams and postgraduate NEET rankings, raising fears that a purely regional-medium track could restrict students seeking specialization or employment outside Karnataka. Dr Purushothama Bilimale, Chairman of the Kannada Development Authority, argued that English replaced earlier Kannada-based medical education but cautioned against making it compulsory since students come from across India; he suggested offering Kannada as an optional subject rather than a mandate.
items.title: RGUHS Weighs Kannada-Medium Medical Degrees Amid Debate Over Bedside Fluency

items.summary: Six months after coming to power in West Bengal, the BJP is struggling to contain allegations of extortion, factionalism, and indiscipline within its ranks. To address these organizational problems and a growing leadership-grassroots divide, party sources say the party has devised an internal monitoring mechanism called Seva Doot. Under this program, scheduled to run from December 1 to December 25—the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee—ministers, MPs, MLAs, and senior functionaries will visit constituencies outside their own to gather public feedback, review the delivery of government welfare schemes, identify administrative shortcomings, and assess the performance of legislators from other constituencies. Constituencies will be assigned randomly so that legislators cannot influence evaluations of their own work. The initiative was discussed at a closed-door organizational meeting held recently at the BJP's Salt Lake headquarters, attended by central observer Sunil Bansal, state president Samik Bhattacharya, and senior functionaries. In the meeting, leadership reportedly warned party functionaries against indiscipline; Bansal told attendees not to behave in ways that force action against them, while expressing displeasure over MLAs sending representatives instead of attending meetings personally. Bhattacharya said he would ask Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari to designate a single minister to communicate the government's official position and warned district leaders that 10 more could be replaced if they failed to perform. The warnings came amid complaints about friction between elected representatives and local organizational leaders, as well as allegations of extortion. Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta earlier this month acknowledged that extortion continued in the state despite the change of power, admitting he had not eliminated it even in his own Rashbehari constituency. Recent incidents include an alleged assault on Debra MLA Subhashis Om following a clash over extortion accusations against rival faction leader Tanmoy Das, and the formation of a three-member committee to investigate the death of Arup Saha after allegedly being assaulted by party workers. The Seva Doot program follows the Seva Setu initiative launched in September around Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday. Party sources say visiting leaders will identify people excluded from welfare schemes, find out why they were left out, work with administration to address grievances, and spend nights at homes of local party workers rather than luxury hotels. The launch of another outreach exercise within months suggests the earlier initiative did not fully achieve its intended purpose.
items.title: Bengal BJP Launches Seva Doot Cross-Constituency Audits to Rein in MLAs

items.summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) has agreed to accept a squadron's worth of delayed Tejas Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Mk-1A fighters from Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) by March 31, 2027. During a high-level review meeting at Air Headquarters last week, HAL officials committed to delivering between 16 and 18 jets by that date, according to unnamed officials familiar with the discussions reported Monday by Hindustan Times.
items.title: HAL to Deliver First Batch of Delayed Tejas LCA Mk-1A Fighters by March 2027

items.summary:
Arion Kurtaj, a 21-year-old member of the Lapsus$ hacking group who leaked footage of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), was released from custody on Monday after receiving a seven-year prison sentence for cyberattacks against major companies. According to the City of London Police, Kurtaj pleaded guilty to six charges at Woolwich Crown Court on Nov. 16 and was sentenced to seven years' imprisonment on Nov. 23.

The court reduced his original nine-year sentence by two years to account for time he had spent under a hospital order, with his previous custody also factored in before he was released on license. In September 2022, Kurtaj hacked into Rockstar Games and stole 90 gameplay videos from the then-unreleased GTA VI, which he subsequently leaked online. Rockstar told a British court in 2023 that recovering from the cyberattack cost it approximately $5 million plus thousands of hours of staff time.

His attacks also targeted telecoms providers BT and EE, fintech company Revolut, and transport platform Uber. Kurtaj pleaded guilty to one count of fraud, four offenses under the Computer Misuse Act 1990, and one offense relating to possession of a mobile phone in prison. He has severe autism and was placed under an indefinite hospital order in December 2023 after being deemed unfit to stand trial; that order was lifted in January 2026, allowing criminal proceedings to resume.

Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said: "Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement." His release came four days after GTA VI launched worldwide on Nov. 19.
items.title: GTA VI hacker released despite being sentenced to seven years in UK prison

items.summary: On Monday, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. The reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, indicated Moscow was thought to be planning such a launch in the coming weeks, which would give it the capability to destroy other satellites. This statement came from NATO chief Mark Rutte as reported by FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher.
items.title: NATO Vows Space Defence After Reports of Russian Nuclear Satellite

items.summary: At a meeting hosted by Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico in Bratislava on Monday, the prime ministers of the Visegrád Four (V4) countries—Hungary's Péter Magyar, Czech Republic's Andrej Babiš, Slovakia's Robert Fico, and Poland's Donald Tusk—together with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker voiced concerns over the European Union's next seven-year budget proposal. The leaders questioned spending priorities and plans to include funding for Ukraine in the draft budget while discussing economic cooperation, migration, and the budget itself. Magyar said his government did not consider the proposal an acceptable starting point for negotiations and wrote to European Council President António Costa explaining that he saw little point in holding a special council meeting scheduled for later in the week as "there is no point spending two days in Brussels not agreeing on anything." Babiš signalled similar concerns, saying he had expected the European Commission to show at least some sign that it wanted to save money and arguing that maintaining a European Parliament in three locations was unnecessary and costly. Slovak PM Fico said the leaders had not adopted a joint position on the budget during Monday's meeting as this had not been the purpose of their discussions, although he noted they were broadly aligned. On funding for Ukraine, Tusk spoke mainly about security, saying Poland was committed to peace but that recent events showed the impact of Russia's invasion of Ukraine on Poland; he underlined the importance of continuing support for Kyiv and argued that the country's ability to defend itself was of strategic significance for Europe's security. Magyar warned that "support for Ukraine should not be included in the EU budget," arguing there was no question that Ukraine deserved solidarity but contending that financial support should not be incorporated into the bloc's budget in a way that would make contributions mandatory for all members, noting Hungary was already providing various forms of assistance to the Ukrainian people and government. Tusk said he did not think it was a good idea for the EU to finance support for Ukraine through joint borrowing—something the Hungarian government has made clear it would not take part in. At a press conference after the meeting, the leaders stressed that regional cooperation was important and achievable given their shared positions on key issues; Fico said the V4 countries and Austria broadly agreed on cohesion policy, migration policy, and agricultural strategies. On illegal migration, all the leaders called for strict rules and consistent enforcement, while Fico praised a plan for some EU member states to establish immigration return hubs in Rwanda. Austrian Chancellor Stocker said it was in Austria's interest to cooperate with its neighbours and wanted the country to be an ally of the V4, adding that closer cooperation would help ensure the rest of the EU better understood developments in central and eastern Europe.
items.title: Visegrád Four Leaders Voice Concerns Over EU Budget Proposal

items.summary: A CGTN opinion piece by doctoral candidate Cao Cong argues that right-wing forces in Japan are increasingly embedding narratives glorifying past aggression into popular culture, contending that such works undermine the international credibility of Japanese culture and erode peace consensus built on honest reckoning with history. The commentary cites several specific controversies: the television drama VIVANT for depicting Chinese characters using torture methods employed by Japanese troops during their invasion; the manga My Hero Academia naming a villain 'Maruta Shiga,' referencing Unit 731's dehumanizing term for experiment victims; and the film The Eternal Zero for centering kamikaze pilots' sacrifices while downplaying Japan's responsibility. It also names cartoonist Yoshinori Kobayashi's On War works as denying or distorting facts including the comfort women system, and notes that a January 2026 planned Pokemon card game event at Yasukuni Shrine was removed after criticism. Cao Cong attributes these claims to his own analysis in the piece rather than established fact. The article states Japan has historical precedents for using creative works to glorify war, citing Momotaro's Sea Eagles (1943) as produced with Navy Ministry support. It reports figures attributed to Japanese government policy documents: a New Cool Japan Strategy target of expanding overseas content sales to 20 trillion yen ($125.83 billion) by 2033, and a fiscal year 2027 Foreign Ministry budget request addressing 'cognitive warfare.' Cao Cong asserts that as reflection on past aggression weakens and perceptions of external threats intensify, right-wing calls for military expansion may gain acceptance, framing historical revisionism as reinforcing neo-militarism. He concludes by calling on international cultural institutions, entertainment companies, media outlets, and research institutions to make historical responsibility part of production, licensing, promotion, and public education.
items.title: CGTN Commentator Warns Japan's Cultural Exports Risk Becoming Vehicles for Historical Revisionism

items.summary: At the FIFA U17 World Cup, Ivory Coast's Under-17 team suffered a 2–1 defeat to Italy in their second group match after opening with a 2–1 win over Uzbekistan. The Ivorians now hold three points from two matches and will face Jamaica in their final group game, where a victory would strengthen their chances of advancing to the next round.
items.title: Ivory Coast U-17s Seek Progression After Narrow Loss to Italy

items.summary: As China's tenure as host of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) organization draws to a close, the Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen has emerged as a pivotal moment. The meeting concluded with participating leaders adopting the Shenzhen Outlook, which is part of a series of outcomes described as historic. In response to these developments, political leaders and scholars from around the world have shared their views on APEC's results.
items.title: Global Leaders and Scholars React to APEC's Historic Shenzhen Outcomes

items.summary:
According to Energy Information Administration (EIA) data, U.S. refiners spent the first eight months of 2026 squeezing less gasoline out of every barrel as they chased higher diesel and jet fuel margins. Average gasoline yields fell below 45% in that period and dropped below the previous five-year low in every month, while jet fuel's share of output topped 12% in March for the first time on record and remained at or above that level through August. Refiners also raised crude processing capacity by 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) in Q2 and another 500,000 bpd in Q3 after a year of operating near maximum capacity.

Bloomberg's Will Kubzansky wrote Monday that the gasoline crack spread—adjusted for real-world crude prices and renewable fuel credits—is now 'barely positive' and has turned negative in some parts of the country. U.S. diesel margins stood above $80 a barrel on Friday, their lowest level since mid-July.

In EIA's weekly report covering the week to November 13, U.S. refinery utilization rose to 95.7%, while gasoline inventories climbed by 5.2 million barrels to 215.9 million barrels—more than three times the 1.6 million barrels analysts polled by Reuters had expected. Distillate stocks rose by 1.6 million barrels to 104.9 million.

Reuters columnist Ron Bousso wrote Monday that U.S. gasoline stocks are now above their five-year average, while distillate inventories sit about 15% below it; the two fuels have moved to opposite ends of the five-year range. Diesel margins fell from a record $118 a barrel in mid-September to about $80, and the U.S. crack spread dropped from a record $72 a barrel to about $41.

Drivers are seeing the decline at the pump: AAA reported that the national average for regular gasoline fell 18 cents in a week to $3.72 a gallon on November 19 (down from $4.30 a month earlier) and slipped further to $3.64 by Monday, though it remains more than 60 cents above a year ago. AAA said prices could fall another 15 cents by Thanksgiving.

Third-quarter results show how far diesel out-earned gasoline before the slide: Valero Energy reported net income of $6.8 billion against $1.1 billion a year earlier, with a refining margin of $39.24 per barrel versus $13.14; on the U.S. Gulf Coast its ultra-low-sulfur diesel margin averaged $72.27 a barrel over Brent (up from $21.05), three times its gasoline margin of $24.08. Marathon Petroleum ran refineries at 100% of crude capacity and lifted its refining and marketing margin to $45.70 a barrel from $17.60; shares of both companies have doubled this year, per the Motley Fool.

The International Energy Agency said in its November Oil Market Report that refining margins weakened almost everywhere in October, with lower gasoline prices weighing on U.S. refiners' profits even as cheaper crude helped them. The agency expects global refinery runs to rise from a seasonal low of 81.3 million bpd in October to 84.7 million bpd in December.

Kubzansky noted that crack spreads could widen again, naming Russia as one catalyst: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on October 30 (per TASS) that Ukrainian drone attacks 'could certainly lead to a decrease in export volumes' of diesel. On November 18, Reuters reported—citing sources—that drone attacks had nearly halved Russia's oil refining in November. Bousso put European diesel futures at around $160 a barrel, down a quarter from the September peak but nearly double their level at the start of the year.

The article also notes that the Middle East situation has not changed: Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have intensified in recent weeks, and disruption to fuel shipments from the Persian Gulf is now in its ninth month.
items.title: U.S. Refiners Sacrifice Gasoline Margins to Chase Diesel and Jet Fuel

items.summary: Saurav Das, co-convener of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), alleged on Monday that immigration officials prevented him from boarding a flight to London for an event at the University of Oxford, as reported by news agency Press Trust of India. According to PTI, Das said his passport was flagged at Delhi airport's immigration counter before he could board the 1 am Britain-bound flight; he had been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union to take part in a panel discussion on the "cockroach movement." In posts on X, Das accused the Modi government of silencing educated voices and being afraid of him speaking at prestigious institutions such as Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, and Edinburgh. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that someone in power was jealous of Das receiving an invitation from Oxford. The CJP accused the government of trying to silence educated voices, while Das maintained that the incident would not deter him from continuing his work or travelling abroad.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das Alleges Passport Flagged, Denied Boarding London Flight

items.summary: At a United Nations Security Council briefing on Monday, Türkiye's permanent representative to the UN, Ahmet Yildiz, said Ankara is developing an effective mechanism to ensure safe navigation of commercial vessels in the Black Sea and maintain uninterrupted flow of food and agricultural supplies. Speaking at a session addressing Ukraine's critical energy infrastructure and Black Sea food lifelines, Yildiz stated that building on Türkiye's experience with the Black Sea Grain Initiative—signed in Istanbul on July 22, 2022 by Russia, Ukraine and Türkiye—the proposed mechanism would serve the interests of all parties, particularly countries most dependent on these supplies. He noted that recalling how the initiative prevented war from spilling into the waterway, Türkiye will leverage its geopolitical location to pursue lasting maritime stability while preventing wider regional escalation, citing Ankara's invocation of Article 19 of the Montreux Convention authorizing closure of the Turkish Straits to belligerent warships. Yildiz also pointed to the Mine Countermeasures Black Sea Task Group established by Türkiye, Romania and Bulgaria as a model for sustainable regional solutions while reaffirming support for Ukraine's independence and territorial integrity and urging direct talks toward peace grounded in international law.
items.title: Türkiye Developing Mechanism for Safe Black Sea Commercial Navigation

items.summary: The Alaska Energy Authority's board unanimously approved a nearly $5 million loan through its Power Project Fund to build an approximately $35 million solar project at the Red Dog zinc mine in Alaska. Tugliq Red Dog will construct, own, and operate the facility and sell electricity to mine operator Teck Alaska. The state's loan review indicates site work began in June and expects the solar array and battery storage to come online in October 2028.
items.title: Alaska Approves Loan for Solar Farm at Red Dog Mine
