Quantum WIY Industries, a joint venture between German defence firm Quantum Systems and Ukraine's WIY Drones, announced on Monday that its SPYS interceptor UAV shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran-5 K5-K attack drone during combat testing in Ukraine. The company said the successful interception occurred while developing and scaling interceptors to defend Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure against Russia's evolving attack systems.

The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, reported that Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn. The agency classified the drone as a compact cruise missile based on its aerodynamic scheme and tactical-technical characteristics, noting it can hit speeds exceeding 450 kph and reach an altitude of 6 km.

The SPYS interceptor is designed to counter both attack and reconnaissance drones while protecting military positions, mobile units, and critical infrastructure. According to WIY Drones, the system reaches speeds of up to around 450 kph with a flight ceiling of 4 km.
items.title: German-Ukrainian SPYS Interceptor Claims First Shot-Down of Russian Jet-Powered Geran-5 K5-K Drone

items.summary: Brian Mundubile, Zambia's main opposition leader and runner-up to President Hakainde Hichilema in the August general election, has been formally indicted on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government. After his campaign documented what he described as serious irregularities in the vote and announced plans to challenge the results in court, Mundubile and his running mate were taken into custody two weeks later and charged with treason alongside 12 others. A magistrate has now submitted the case to the High Court for trial, though no date for the proceedings has been set. The former government minister has previously denied any wrongdoing; if convicted, the defendants face up to life in prison. Rights groups have accused Zambian authorities of political repression following an election that international observer missions said was marred by irregularities.
items.title: Zambia's Opposition Leader Mundubile Indicted on Treason Charges

items.summary: For the first time since 2009, COP31 ended without a deal to advance an energy transition after participating countries failed to agree on key aspects of that agreement. Disagreements centered most notably on financial commitments for developing nations and on attributing climate change to oil and gas production. Negotiators went into overtime on the final day discussing what was supposed to be a deal focused on climate attribution, fresh funding for developing countries, and carbon capture—yet many countries declined to endorse blaming fossil fuels or committing further billions amid strained state budgets. The European Union, long the most generous global climate finance donor but facing tight money due to soaring fuel prices, high gas costs, refining shortages, and heavy spending needs on direct subsidies and tax cuts for hydrocarbons it is trying to phase out, had already signaled its reluctance before COP31 began; EU climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said in late October that the possibility of fresh EU money for emission reduction projects was “dead in the water,” citing two years without global progress on emissions. The EU also reportedly felt other wealthy regions were not doing enough in climate finance, according to a Bloomberg report from last month. On the final day, environment minister of Panama said as quoted by Reuters that it is “not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels,” echoing attitudes across EU capitals after Brussels rejected the draft over its absence of specific references naming hydrocarbons as culprits behind global warming. The president of COP31, Turkey’s climate change minister, said as quoted by Al Jazeera that “there are parties in this hall who oppose this text” and that decisions had not been adopted because there was no consensus; Ireland’s energy minister added as quoted by the same publication that they would not endorse a cover decision or an “Antalya Pact” failing to mention fossil fuels. The EU’s stance drew criticism from Friends of the Earth, whose head called it hypocritical for insisting on naming oil and gas as guilty while consuming more of those commodities, and Asad Rehman also said as quoted by Al Jazeera that there has been a litany of broken promises largely from developed countries with blame to go around. The article notes that some African resource-rich countries have recently reconsidered the benefits of climate loans and grants tied to strings banning them from benefiting from their own resources, while the EU’s oil and gas struggles amid sanctions, wars, and climate ambitions are compounded by the U.S. no longer being a staunch transition ally as it was two years ago; author Irina Slav wrote for Oilprice.com that COP31’s failure “was only to be expected” as cold reality overtook hopes.
items.title: COP31 Ends Without Deal Over Climate Finance and Fossil Fuel Blame

items.summary: In a new episode of Politics Weekly, Pippa Crerar speaks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham about his plans to win parliamentary backing for a new EU deal. While Burnham has set out these intentions, the various options for how Britain could rejoin the EU—referred to as 'Breturn'—will not be outlined until December. The podcast explores how he hopes to convince the public that reversing Brexit is worth the effort.
items.title: Guardian Podcast: Tactics Burnham Will Use to Sell His EU Plans

items.summary: Mongabay Kids has launched Wild Guardians, a free multimedia educational series aimed at upper elementary (fourth and fifth grade) students to connect them with nature and inspire environmental stewardship. The initiative features five-minute videos, illustrated comics, and standards-aligned lessons across three conservation topics: restoring habitat for giraffes in Tanzania, the role of wild bees, and protecting waterways in Chattanooga, Tennessee. In the Tanzania segment, primary school students grow food for giraffes while learning about tree planting, cleanups, and habitat restoration; in Tennessee, elementary students explore their local creek and watershed home to wildlife such as the hellbender and crawfish, learning how waterways connect landscapes from mountains to sea; and a wild bee safari teaches children that more than 20,000 species of bees exist—most being wild bees that do not produce honey—and explains their importance for pollination. Wild Guardians education lead Emily Townsend said the resources let students learn about conservation in their local community alongside math, English language arts, and social studies, with each toolkit including a video, comic, and interdisciplinary lessons chosen by teachers to engage students as stewards of their community. Mallory Lindsay of The Chuck & Ernestina Kreutzkamp Foundation's Earth Focus Initiative, the project's primary funder, described Wild Guardians as meaningful for helping children move from learning about wildlife to understanding they can actively protect it, connecting classroom knowledge with local species and environmental challenges. Veila Makundi and Monica Bond of the Wild Nature Institute, whose work is featured in the Tanzania video, said the project provides a practical toolkit that gives kids hope by enabling action for nature.
items.title: Mongabay Kids Launches Wild Guardians Education Initiative

items.summary: On Nov 24, Asian shares surged following a Wall Street rally triggered by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and renewed optimism in the battered AI trade. MSCI's broadest Asia-Pacific index outside Japan climbed 4.6%, bouncing back from an eight-month low for its biggest single-day gain since July 31. The Nikkei added 4.5% after traders returned from a local holiday, South Korea's KOSPI jumped 7.5%, and Taiwanese shares rose 9.1%. Nvidia itself surged 31.5% on Nov 23 — its biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years — restoring nearly US$1 trillion (S$1.3 trillion) in value to the company, while the Nasdaq 100 jumped more than 6% as AI-industry companies rallied broadly.
items.title: Asian Stocks Rally as Jensen Huang's Nvidia Return Revives AI Trade

items.summary: Hangzhou-based AI start-up DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's fortune climbed to US$55 billion (S$71 billion) after the company completed its latest fund-raising, drawing investment from industrial tycoons and cementing his status as the world's richest creator of AI models. According to registry filings, Liang's stake in the firm fell to 67.4% from 81.65% in June. items.title: DeepSeek Founder Liang Wenfeng Worth US$55 Billion After Latest Fund-Raising

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued a statement warning investors about fraudsters who impersonate Sebi-registered intermediaries to lure them into purported institutional trading opportunities. According to the regulator, these scammers often portray international stock markets as more lucrative than Indian markets, offer stock and index recommendations, direct investors to unauthorized trading platforms, and ask them to transfer funds to designated bank accounts held in the names of unregistered entities. Sebi identified several warning signs that investors should watch for, including invitations to closed social media groups from unknown sources, administrators using international mobile numbers, and promises of recovering losses in Indian portfolios through investments in foreign markets.
items.title: Sebi Warns of Fake WhatsApp and Telegram Trading Groups

items.summary: Singapore actor Andi Lim, nominated for Best Supporting Actor at Sunday's (Nov 22) Golden Horse Awards for his role in Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers, said he could not borrow any clothes to wear because of having just over 1,300 Instagram followers. He revealed this in an interview with #JustSwipeLah. Lim wore a tuxedo lent to him by Leslie Chia, founder and creative director of Singapore bespoke menswear label PIMABS, whom he described as his cousin's classmate; Chia had also loaned Lim an outfit for the Berlin International Film Festival. Lim said he wanted to dress formally out of respect for the black-tie event, noting the tuxedo was not traditional in cut and featured a hand-tied bow tie that could be adjusted in size. Though Lim lost Best Supporting Actor to Hong Kong boy band Mirror's Anson Kong (who won for We're Nothing At All), his film received seven nominations and won Best Original Film Score for Singaporean musician Kin Leonn and Belgian-Taiwanese composer Thomas Foguenne.
items.title: Golden Horse nominee Andi Lim couldn't borrow an outfit for the awards show because he has too few Instagram followers

items.summary: An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that CEO Jensen Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia's board that reinstating the company's cofounder poses no national security risk. In parallel, several probes continue: the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers while circumventing US export restrictions; the Securities and Exchange Commission has reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia's accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders; California's attorney general has opened an investigation into the company's chip exports and shareholder disclosures. Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said that because the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, these federal probes might not result in much, though he also warned of a possible 'boomerang' if Trump becomes estranged from Huang. On December 1, Huang will explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing before three House committees, and on December 3 he will testify before a Senate committee in a livestreamed hearing.
items.title: Questions linger after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

items.summary: The US Commerce Department published a notice on Monday adding Singapore-based company Megaspeed, along with its subsidiaries in Thailand and Malaysia, to the trade blacklist. As an Nvidia partner under investigation since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, Megaspeed will now require Commerce approval for US exports that is likely to be denied. The action follows revelations reported by The New York Times on Monday that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed's controlling shareholder who reportedly maintained contact with an official of China's top spy agency while having a relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was alleged to be a Beijing spy; China has called the accusations groundless. Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said his country is conducting its own investigation into Megaspeed but is not involved in the US inquiry regarding Jensen Huang's role, noting that Singapore previously investigated Alice Huang and found no basis for prosecution. Senator Pete Ricketts stated on social media that Commerce still needs to explain to Congress why the action took so long. The New York Times reported that Alice Huang kept contact with a Chinese spy agency official for more than a year while carrying out her relationship with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people familiar with US intelligence reports. The US Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China and issued a joint statement last week saying it would bring the full extent of the law against any criminal conduct; Megaspeed did not immediately respond but had said earlier this month that it conducts lawful business complying with US export controls, added that Alice Huang officially left in August 2025. Nvidia has formed an export control committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. As Semafor notes, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faced pressure to act since the Jensen Huang relationship became public; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this month his agency along with the Pentagon, State Department and US Trade Representative's office had wanted Megaspeed on the blacklist for months but that Commerce holds authority over it. Bessent publicly complained about the delay and questioned whether Nvidia knew of its client and made a robust effort to prevent leakage through pass-through shell companies.
items.title: US Adds Nvidia-Linked Firm Megaspeed to Trade Blacklist

items.summary: On Monday, Nvidia's board of directors unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company's chief executive officer and president. President Trump has publicly claimed credit for brokering the deal behind his return. items.summary:
On Monday (Nov 23), US lawmakers from both parties sharply criticized Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, calling for Congress to tighten restrictions on China's access to the company's advanced AI chips and scrutinize the circumstances surrounding his return. President Donald Trump said he pressed Nvidia's board to bring Huang back while lawmakers seek answers about why the board reversed its earlier decision not to reinstate him; Senator John Curtis asked what changed after the board had previously stated it did not intend to reappoint Huang.

Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Tom Cotton, a Republican, called on Congress to pass the Chip Security Act, which would require chipmakers to track advanced AI processors and notify the government if they suspect chips have reached prohibited users. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts described the reinstatement as 'reckless,' saying Nvidia's board still owes Congress answers about compliance with US export controls.

Huang is scheduled to testify on Dec 3 before the Senate Banking Committee, whose Republican Chair Tim Scott announced Monday, while lawmakers probe allegations about Huang's ties to a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Senator Pete Ricketts said the reinstatement 'doesn't excuse' Huang from testifying and is pushing for Congress to pass the Match Act, which would pressure US allies such as ASML in the Netherlands and Tokyo Electron in Japan to restrict sales of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China.

Representative Jim Himes, top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, said Huang remains expected to appear for a closed-door interview on Dec 1 with three House panels. Incoming Speaker Hakeem Jeffries said Congress should include 'ironclad' legislation in the annual defense Bill to prevent AI technology from reaching China; Nvidia did not immediately comment on the criticism.
items.title: US Lawmakers Criticize Nvidia's Decision to Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

items.summary: Jensen Huang has returned as CEO of Nvidia after resigning last week amid revelations that he had a series of extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, who is alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. US President Donald Trump took credit for the move, telling CNBC that he spoke to and convinced the board — even though Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones had previously ruled out rehiring him. Olivia Shen, director of the Strategic Technologies Program at the US Studies Centre, described the intervention as 'telling,' saying it felt like Jensen Huang is a protected species because the Nvidia reinstatement video stated they received advice from highest levels of the US government.
items.title: Trump Intervenes to Reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: President Donald Trump intervened to restore Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, an action that offered an early indication of how he can continue to wield power during the traditionally lame-duck phase of a presidency despite losing control of Congress to Democrats. Days after the Nvidia board ruled out restoring Huang following damaging revelations about his relations with an alleged Chinese spy and other women, Trump forcefully made the case for Huang's return in a press conference on Friday. He then dispatched key members of his administration throughout the weekend to convince the board to reverse its position in an announcement shortly before the stock market opened on Monday.
items.title: Trump Intervenes to Restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Tuku Nkosiyaphantsi, a 50-year-old father from Kokstad in KwaZulu-Natal province, learned that his 27-year-old daughter Okuhle had been killed after two neighbours told him she had been reported missing on Facebook and showed him a photo of what appeared to be an injured woman. Upon closer inspection he recognized the body as Okuhle's; confirming her death with a police officer, who said her remains had been dumped near a river in Kokstad, Tuku could not identify the mutilated and badly beaten corpse until Monday morning because the morgue was closed for the weekend. Okuhle left two children aged nine and three and was studying civil engineering. Months after her killing no one has been arrested, prompting Tuku to say he wishes police would investigate rather than remain silent about his daughter's death; he believes they failed to review CCTV footage from a local government building that may have shown who she was with on the day she disappeared, though such footage is wiped every seven days. The BBC approached the South African Police Service for comment but received no response at publication time. Okuhle is among 581 women killed in South Africa between July and September according to the South African Police Service; overall there were 5,590 murders - 204 fewer than the same period last year. It is the first time police have broken down murders by gender, so it remains unclear whether the number of women killed represents an increase or decrease on previous years. A renewed national outcry about violence against women has followed this summer's discovery of partially naked and bruised bodies of 12 women dumped in public areas in Ekurhuleni, a district east of Johannesburg; South Africa is noted for having one of the highest rates of gender-based violence and femicide - the intentional killing of a woman or girl - in the world. In response to this summer's killings President Cyril Ramaphosa promised safety audits across every municipality to identify dangerous spaces for women as well as an increased police presence in worst-affected areas, though Tuku says he has little faith anything will change and feels his community is ignored by the government despite those promises; earlier this month Ramaphosa said extra money would be allocated in February's budget to address gender-based violence and that police numbers had been increased over the last three years with more visible policing. In Kokstad, five women and three very young children were found killed between January and October this year with arrests taking place only in two of those cases; in response community members set up street patrols and a curfew for women and children, with children told to stay indoors by sunset since June and women by 21:00. Kamvalethu Cetywayo, 34, from a local neighbourhood watch group, leads around 15 men who patrol crime hotspots at night including areas where bodies have been found or trouble reported; patrols tend to occur between Thursday and Sunday because that is when people drink alcohol most heavily according to him, with most patrollers carrying sticks, whips and torches while he holds a licensed gun. The group will call police for back-up, and Kamvalethu says the curfew helps keep women safe, is voluntary, and temporary until killers are arrested; if people refuse there is nothing they can do in his view. Not all victims are attacked at night or on streets: Kgothatso Mojela was kidnapped on her way to work in 2018 in Kempton Park when a taxi driver locked the doors and drove in the wrong direction, punching and slapping her after she said he had missed a turn; forcing the passenger door open, she threw herself out of the moving taxi badly injuring her knee and causing nerve damage to her eyes before two nearby security guards came to her aid. Her attacker was later jailed for several crimes including what he did to her but released last year, leaving Kgothatso now 35 fearing for her life; in its wake she bought an imitation gun to scare off would-be attackers, stopped running alone, and insists on someone accompanying her when meeting clients she has not met before at work. Such precautions are familiar to many women in South Africa: in September police urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone particularly in isolated areas after 38-year-old mother Elizabeth Moselakgomo vanished on 9 September while out running, her badly bruised and partially clothed body found dumped near a busy motorway three days later. Her disappearance resonated within South Africa's running community including sisters Zonke and Zama Mthethwa who started The Pack women's running group in Johannesburg nine years ago; runners across the city joined search efforts following Elizabeth's disappearance and took part in protests calling for violence against women to end, with her group now carrying pepper spray and whistles during runs, getting cars to follow them, and offering self-defence coaching. Following her ordeal Kgothatso moved from Kempton Park closer to her parents; her mother, a community activist, recently organised a prayer march to remember killed women where Kgothatso told her story for the first time, saying survivors are not dirty, broken beyond repair, to blame, or alone.
items.title: Dad who discovered daughter's murder on Facebook feels ignored by South African police

Asian shares surged on Tuesday after Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, sparking a relief rally in the battered AI trade. MSCI's broadest Asia-Pacific index outside Japan climbed 4.6 per cent to its biggest single-day gain in two weeks and an eight-month low; Japan's Nikkei rose 4.5 per cent, South Korea's KOSPI jumped 7.5 per cent, and Taiwan's shares leapt 9.1 per cent. The rally followed Nvidia's Monday surge of 31.5 per cent — its largest daily percentage gain in 23 years — which restored nearly $1 trillion to the company's value, while the Nasdaq 100 rose more than 6 per cent.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said Huang's return eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade "at least at the margins," though concerns remained over slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth. He also flagged upcoming US interest rate policy uncertainty as a risk, with investors set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data ahead of the Fed's final 2026 meeting.

The rebound eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving bets for near-term Federal Reserve tightening: traders now price a hike at December's meeting as certain versus 89 per cent odds on Friday. The market-implied chance of a 50-basis-point increase sits around 5 per cent. US Treasury yields rose — the benchmark 10-year note reached 4.94 per cent and the 2-year note climbed to 4.69 per cent — while the dollar hovered near a more than 19-month high against the euro.

In commodities, oil fell more than 3 per cent on rising Middle East supplies that offset shipping and refinery attack worries; Brent crude settled at $89.50 a barrel after dropping 3.5 per cent to $89.37 Monday. Spot gold recovered from a more than one-year low, up 0.7 per cent to $3,657.97 an ounce as investors bought the dip.
items.title: Asian Stocks Rally as Jensen Huang's Nvidia Return Revives AI Trade

President Donald Trump said he personally convinced Nvidia's board of directors to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12 amid reports of a trio of extramarital affairs. In a CNBC interview Monday, Trump stated plainly that he 'spoke to them' and 'convinced them,' framing the reinstatement as essential to U.S. AI ambitions and warning that losing Huang—a talent officials feared could be poached by a Chinese firm—risked putting America behind Beijing in the field.

The board's reversal was notable because it had insisted days earlier that it was not considering such a move, even as Trump pushed for it and thousands signed an online petition. Trump urged reinstatement over several days, arguing Huang should be restored given his role as a trusted White House adviser on AI, a major donor to the president's ballroom project, and a growing personal investor whose disclosed Nvidia holdings rose from USD 615,000–USD 1.3 million at end of 2024 to between USD 12.5 million and USD 58 million by end of 2025 (per his June 2026 financial disclosure). A White House spokesman said the portfolio is independently managed through discretionary accounts that automatically replicate recognized indexes, with no family input.

Trump cited falling AI stocks after Huang's ouster as part of his case. Advisers Vice President JD Vance, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent—who had called for a 'dramatic shake-up' at Nvidia—also helped persuade the board; Vance stepped up involvement over the weekend as an effective emissary to overcome reservations.

Trump downplayed the infidelity angle, noting Huang apologized to the company, country, family, and wife. The scandal carried added complexity because one affair involved Alice Huang of Megaspeed, whom U.S. officials suspect was a China intelligence asset (Beijing denies it). Trump said U.S. officials assured Nvidia that Huang posed no national security risk.

Trump distinguished this case from other corporate scandals—citing McDonald's Steve Easterbrook, BP's Bernard Looney, and Intel's Brian Krzanich—as emphasizing Huang's 'vast amount of knowledge' in a technology shaping nearly every facet of life, while expressing concern he could be scooped up by China. He said the scandal would ultimately prove 'a net positive.'

Trump marveled that the S&P 500 leapt 4.7 per cent Monday following Huang's return, reflecting his broader reliance on market movements to validate leadership and shape policies like tariffs and Iran policy.

He views AI investment as central to economic growth: tech firms spent roughly USD 800 billion this year building data centers with Nvidia chips and related equipment, projected to total USD 10.3 trillion from 2025 through 2032 (about 3.6 per cent of the economy), per Columbia University economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh.

Trump's intervention drew bipartisan criticism: former House Speaker Newt Gingrich questioned returning Huang amid suspicions about the Chinese spy, and Sen. Tim Scott announced Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3. Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries criticized the reinstatement, with Jeffries calling it 'indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.' Trump nonetheless argued the spotlight showed how advanced Nvidia is under his leadership.
items.title: Trump Persuades Nvidia Board to Reinstate Jensen Huang

Nvidia's board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, ending an 11-day interim leadership period under Colette Kress. According to a CNBC report, the announcement came after Huang stepped down earlier in November following revelations of extramarital relationships and sparked a strong market reaction: Nvidia shares surged 31% on Monday while the Nasdaq rose more than 6%. Alongside his return as CEO, president and board director with immediate effect, Nvidia confirmed that Kress will continue as CFO. The board accepted Huang's resignation on November 11 and appointed Kress, 59, who joined Nvidia in September 2013 after roles at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments, to lead the company during a period of uncertainty.

Kress holds approximately 4.775 million Nvidia shares directly and indirectly, valued at about $778 million based on Monday's closing price. During her interim leadership she sought to reassure investors by raising Nvidia's fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to roughly 75%, up from an earlier estimate of 70%, while repeatedly stressing that operations remained "business as usual" and characterizing customer demand for AI products as rising with major clients remaining committed. At an all-hands employee meeting after Huang's exit, she encouraged staff to focus on the future and highlighted upcoming pay increases.

Not everyone shared criticism of Kress; according to CNBC, one former Nvidia employee praised her for handling the crisis with "skill and grace" and described her as a "fantastic CFO" who retains Huang's trust. In an official statement confirming his reinstatement, Huang thanked Kress for leading the company during his absence.

Huang's return does not end the investigation into him; a committee of independent directors working with independent counsel is continuing to look into foreign intelligence reports, and Huang said he fully supports it and will cooperate. Nvidia has added new oversight layers including a National Security and Export Control Committee made up only of independent directors, additional national security counsel who will hire specialist advisers, and a search for a new Chief Compliance Officer reporting to the board's Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. The company said it would keep cooperating with ongoing government investigations, with Huang and general counsel Tim Teter scheduled to answer questions from US House committees behind closed doors on December 1 and 2.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and Confirms Colette Kress Remains CFO

On Monday, November 23, Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang following a controversy over his alleged extramarital affair with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence and concerns about the possible diversion of Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China. items.summary: In an interview published Tuesday with the South China Morning Post, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said that new U.S. export curbs on advanced AI chips aimed at restricting their use by China will not deter Malaysia from working with Beijing and Chinese firms. Anwar told the South China Morning Post that Malaysia is not leaning toward either China or the United States, though he found it generally easier to deal with Beijing due to existing cultural and regional ties. The new U.S. rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to Southeast Asian countries such as Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, which Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models. The company states that these new connections let it leverage data within its ecosystem to provide experiences it says rivals cannot match, while noting that connecting Wallet and Drive is optional and that Personal Intelligence can be turned on or off at any time. Regarding Wallet, Google says linking the service lets users track financial goals, cut spending, and make better use of credit card rewards, adding that AI Mode will only read information from connected accounts and cannot move or manage money. On Drive, Google claims important project or decision-related information is often spread across documents and spreadsheets, so connecting Drive allows AI to draw on those files for more relevant answers such as a tailored tax-season plan. The company also says users can now share context between the Gemini app and Search's AI Mode in both directions, meaning an idea explored in one will not require starting over in the other. Google further states that users will soon be able to view the context used by AI Mode through a new 'Personalization' icon appearing below responses, and announced on Monday that more personally relevant responses tailored to recent search context are expected in both AI Overviews and AI Mode.

Satyaki Savarkar, the paternal grandnephew of freedom fighter Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi demanding an unconditional apology and correction over remarks about his ancestor in her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love. The notice was issued by advocate Sangram Kolhatkar on Satyaki's behalf and requires the demands be met within 15 days, warning that non-compliance could lead to legal proceedings before a competent court or authority.

The objection centers on two statements in the book. On page 201, the memoir states that while Congress freedom fighters endured British imprisonment, RSS ideologues like Savarkar were writing mercy petitions and colluding with colonial authorities as informers. Satyaki alleges this creates an unsupported impression of collaboration or informing against Indian freedom fighters, disputing it on historical grounds including Savarkar's prolonged imprisonment in the Cellular Jail in the Andaman Islands.

On page 443, the book describes Savarkar as articulating a vision viewing India primarily as a nation where Hindus are supreme—an outlook attributed to Hindutva and the Sangh Parivar. The notice argues this oversimplifies his political philosophy and should be considered within its proper historical, intellectual, and political context.

The two statements together allegedly present a distorted account of Savarkar's role in the freedom struggle and mislead readers about his legacy. To support Savarkar's stature as a patriot, the notice cites government recognition during former prime minister Indira Gandhi's tenure, including a commemorative postage stamp issued in his honor and her personal contribution of Rs 11,000 from her bank account toward the Swatantryaveer Savarkar Rashtriya Smarak. It asks Sonia to explain how these statements reconcile with such records.

The notice demands an unconditional apology plus public clarification explaining the historical basis, context, and intended meaning of the statements, along with acknowledgment and correction of any inaccuracies or misleading implications. It also requests that appropriate steps be taken in consultation with HarperCollins Publishers India—Sonia Gandhi's publisher—to correct, qualify, or withdraw the objectionable statements from subsequent editions, reprints, and electronic versions.

The memoir was reportedly released on November 10, and Satyaki said he recently came across it before being disturbed by the statements concerning his ancestor. PTI reported on the notice.
items.title: Savarkar's Grandnephew Serves Legal Notice to Sonia Gandhi Over Memoir Remarks

items.summary: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of India's Union Home Ministry anti-cybercrime wing, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), issued an advisory on Monday warning that a logged-in WhatsApp Web session left open on a public computer or shared device could allow cybercriminals to hijack accounts. The unit said such sessions could be used to gain unauthorized access and let malicious actors read private messages, send communications while impersonating the account holder, view contact lists and group conversations, and exploit the user's trusted identity to carry out fraud, phishing and social-engineering attacks. I4C cautioned that simply closing a browser window or tab does not end an authenticated session, advising users instead to manually log out after each use—particularly on office computers, shared systems, public devices, cyber cafes, kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers or other untrusted machines—and to avoid conducting official, sensitive work involving government, organizational, financial or confidential information through WhatsApp Web. When use is unavoidable, the unit recommended using incognito and private browsing modes, keeping devices, operating systems and browsers secure with updated security software while avoiding suspicious downloads, unknown files and cracked software, and treating unexpected messages sent from an account or unusual replies as serious signs of compromise.
items.title: India's I4C Warns WhatsApp Web Sessions Can Enable Account Hijacking

The Supreme Court on Monday directed that priority be given to appeals from 22 lakh people, out of a total of 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll. The court sought the state government's response to allegations that voters deleted during the SIR exercise are being denied ration and benefits under various social welfare schemes.

The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said even among the 22 lakh appeals, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) should be heard ahead of others, given the upcoming civic elections. The court also directed that the Calcutta High Court chief justice, in consultation with the Election Commission, increase the number of tribunals currently at 19 to handle the 38 lakh appeals filed after SIR over deletions related to voters declared absent, shifted, duplicate or dead, or flagged for 'logical discrepancy' connected to mapping. The bench further asked the Election Commission to requisition additional space for housing these tribunals.

The direction followed remarks by advocate Prashant Bhushan, who told the court that of 1.4 lakh appeals decided so far by the tribunals appointed after SIR, more than 90% have been allowed, restoring names in the electoral roll. Bhushan said this was a strong indicator based on a large sample size to persuade the top court to direct those whose names were deleted be permitted to vote in upcoming elections.

Bhushan, supported by senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan, told the court that although it had clarified deletion of electoral roll names would have no consequence beyond voting—including regarding citizenship—the state government has been denying deleted voters ration through the public distribution system (PDS) and benefits under social welfare schemes such as Annapurna Yojana. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta countered these were bald assertions, alleging petitioners had cited no example to substantiate their claims.

The CJI-led bench asked the state government to file a response to the allegations. Separately, the Supreme Court postponed to Wednesday its hearing on the state government's appeal challenging an interim order of a Calcutta High Court division bench that restrained the state Election Commission from announcing a schedule for KMC polls, in which wards were increased from 144 to 209 by an amending Act. Mehta said the high court mistakenly concluded the state government lacked jurisdiction over increasing ward numbers and adjusting boundaries.
items.title: Supreme Court Prioritizes Appeals to Restore West Bengal Voter Names

items.summary: A study titled 'Beyond Publication Bias: Characterizing and Understanding Missing Results in Economics,' authored by Fernando Hoces de la Guardia, Edward Miguel, Gufran Pathan, Akash Shaji, Viviane Helena Silva da Rocha, Erik Ø. Sørensen, and Bertil Tungodden (NBER Working Paper 36044), measures missing research results at the hypothesis level to examine under-reporting in economics. Across 5,057 pre-registered hypotheses from 317 studies registered on the American Economic Association RCT Registry between 2015 and 2017, only 42% had publicly available results eight to nine years after pre-registration. Among those available results, 64% were null findings, with little evidence that null results are disproportionately missing from publication. The study found no significant effect of raising awareness alone on the share of hypotheses with available results, and additional research assistance provided no further improvement over direct engagement.
items.title: Study Finds Extensive Missing Results in Economics Research

items.summary: In NBER Working Paper 36045 (2026), Myra Mohnen and Joshua S. Gans study how artificial intelligence shapes whether scientists extend or deepen scientific knowledge, using structural biology as a case where experiments determine a protein's three-dimensional structure and function. They link 530,471 proteins to the experiments run on them between 2017 and 2025, then compare experimental activity after AlphaFold2's 2021 release across proteins with more versus less confident predictions. The authors find that where AI predictions are more confident, the experimental record adds fewer first structures for proteins far from any relative of known structure, while it adds more follow-up experiments on proteins whose structure is already known — a rise largest for proteins surrounded by relatives of known structure. A model of experimental choice explains this pattern as AlphaFold2 deepening existing knowledge rather than extending it: a prediction replaces an experiment that would establish a protein's structure and lowers the cost of experiments that build on that structure.
items.title: How AI Impacts the Quest for Knowledge: Evidence from AlphaFold2

items.summary: In response to a letter by writer Tiffany Ong Rou Ying published on Nov 8 arguing that artificial intelligence must preserve human connection in the classroom, Lee Lin Yee of the Ministry of Education (MOE) affirmed that teachers remain central to assessing and guiding students' learning even with AI. The MOE stated it understands AI use should be judicious to preserve human agency, independent thinking, and individual voice, while being mindful of pitfalls such as over-reliance. Teachers exercise professional judgment on when to withhold or use AI and how it should be used so that students develop personal voice and creativity while strengthening subject mastery; the MOE provides guidelines ensuring AI is introduced gradually in a developmentally and age-appropriate manner. The role of teachers remains critical even as AI is used selectively to augment teaching—for example, by expediting analysis of student responses at individual and class levels, identifying common misconceptions, and generating suggestions for teachers—while teachers draw on their professional knowledge to review and finalise personalised feedback, track learning progress, adjust instruction, and remain responsible for assessing students. The MOE confirmed that all assessment scripts will be reviewed by teachers so AI supports rather than replaces teachers' judgment. Students learn to use AI safely, responsibly, and effectively through cyberwellness lessons and programmes such as Code for Fun, developing these skills when using AI across subjects. Acknowledging that students may have different experiences with AI in schools, the MOE encourages them to share feedback with teachers and will continue enhancing AI literacy development efforts so students can use technology purposefully while understanding its limitations and risks. The writer's suggestion to give students opportunities to share views on AI implementation was welcomed; the MOE said it would work with schools to gather perspectives from teachers, students, and parents as it continues reviewing and adjusting its approach to AI in education and AI literacy development.
items.title: MOE: Teachers Remain Central to Assessment as AI Augments Learning

items.summary: At a United Nations Security Council briefing on Monday, India's Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Black Sea, stressing that safe navigation through international waterways must be restored amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Addressing the high-level session, Ambassador Parvathaneni said the war, now in its fifth year, has far-reaching consequences due to interconnected global supply chains, noting India's readiness to contribute to efforts toward a peaceful resolution and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for moving from 'endless war to the end of war.' He highlighted that armed conflicts disrupt agriculture, displace communities, damage infrastructure, and hinder humanitarian access, with consequences extending globally through disruptions to energy, fertiliser, transport, and agricultural trade while disproportionately impacting the Global South. Parvathaneni emphasized the Security Council's need to prioritise humanitarian access, protection of civilian infrastructure, and freedom of navigation so that humanitarian supplies and legitimate trade are not affected. He underscored the Black Sea region's importance to global food security, noting it and India together account for almost a fifth of global cereal production, while Russia and Ukraine combined accounted for nearly a quarter of global exports of wheat, maize, and barley. The Indian envoy cited India's humanitarian assistance—wheat supplies to Afghanistan, rice to Sudan, and aid to Palestine—and stressed that the Global South is disproportionately affected by food, fuel, and fertiliser crises from conflicts, with energy shortages intensifying concerns; he referenced External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's observation at last month's G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting that fertiliser shortages stem partly from the Black Sea and partly from the Gulf and Red Sea. Parvathaneni recalled the 1943 Bengal famine, which killed over three million people in India, as a reminder of distant conflicts' devastating human costs. He detailed attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea involving four ships: MV Omorfi (attacked July 18), MV Royad Mammadov (October), and MV Golden Leo and MV AGN RAGNAR, resulting in four dead and two missing Indian seafarers; he thanked partner countries for repatriating injured seafarers. Parvathaneni called for an end to targeting commercial shipping and restoration of safe navigation through international waterways at the earliest, noting India's efforts to strengthen maritime safety cooperation, including launching the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers with Liberia during earlier this month's UN high-level week. The voluntary mechanism supports the International Maritime Organisation and International Labour Organisation in addressing shipping safety and security; Parvathaneni said New Delhi is working directly with both sides on Black Sea shipping and grain export corridor safety, reiterating support for an early end to the conflict and 'enduring peace.'
items.title: India Calls for End to Black Sea Shipping Attacks at UN Security Council

items.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly ordered residents of Ulleung Island to seek shelter underground after multiple Russian warplanes entered the country's air identification zone, described as the latest in a string of similar regional incidents. An air raid warning issued Tuesday for the estimated 9,000 people living on Ulleung Island—located about 130 kilometers east of the Korean Peninsula—was lifted minutes after it was initially posted on a local disaster portal. The Russian jets entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) and flew near the island, prompting South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff to deploy its fighter jets in response. In a statement, the JCS said 'The aircraft left following our military measures,' adding that there was no violation of South Korean airspace; it noted that the KADIZ is not territorial airspace but an area where aircraft are expected to identify themselves as they approach. Jang Do-young, a Joint Chiefs spokesperson, told a briefing that the Russian military aircraft had approached Ulleung Island 'to the point where it was just short of entering our airspace,' and said South Korea issued the alert preemptively given how quickly military aircraft travel; he added that such incidents have occurred multiple times but are rare for authorities to issue warnings in response. The military declined to elaborate on how close the jets flew before departing. South Korea plans to summon Russia's military attache to protest the flights, according to the Defense Ministry.
items.title: South Korea Scrambles Jets After Russian Warplanes Enter Air Zone

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued an advisory cautioning investors about the risks of relying on grey market premiums (GMP) to gauge initial public offering prices. Sebi explained that GMP transactions occur before a stock's formal listing, take place outside the exchange framework, are not subject to regulatory oversight, and carry neither settlement guarantees nor investor protection. The regulator also stated that these transactions do not follow any formal price discovery process. In its advisory, Sebi said that publishing such pre-listing premium figures could be detrimental to investors' interests and contrary to transparency and accountability principles in the securities market. Consequently, the regulator called for discontinuing the publication of grey market premium figures through any mode or platform across the securities market.
items.title: Sebi Warns Against Relying on Grey Market Premium as IPO Price Indicator

items.summary: Cameron Munster said he declined Melbourne Storm's latest contract offer, describing it as "disappointing." His teammate Harry Grant met with the Gold Coast last week, and Stefano Utoikamanu has been linked with the Sydney Roosters while remaining off contract for next season. Separately, in a final score result, the Rabbitohs lost 10-20 to the Knights.
items.title: Munster Rejects Melbourne Storm Contract Offer as 'Disappointing'

items.summary: On Monday, Cockroach Janta Party convenor and investigative journalist Saurav Das alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter of Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London at 1 am. In a social media post, Das said he had been invited by prestigious universities including Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), and Edinburgh to deliver talks on what he called the 'cockroach movement,' which concerns youth protests in India. He stated that an 'anti-intellectual government' was afraid of him traveling to these institutions. Hours later, Cockroach Janta Party leader Ratna Singh said she too had been invited to speak at the Oxford Union but her visa had been rejected a few days earlier; she added that Das's denial raises troubling questions about freedom of expression and space for young voices in India. On Monday, party founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that someone 'in power was jealous' of Das receiving an invitation from the University of Oxford. The Cockroach Janta Party political campaign had named Das as its chief spokesperson on June 3, days ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, then Union education minister, over alleged irregularities in conducting competitive examinations; Pradhan resigned on July 25 after the protest spread to other parts of the country following a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi. Das was a key leader of those protests and held discussions with the Union government along with another campaign spokesperson, Ashutosh Ranka. On October 13, Das and Ranka were detained for trespassing on Jantar Mantar and waving the national flag amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in revising the voter roll; they had 'sneaked into' Jantar Mantar to oppose authorities' decision to denotify the area as a designated protest site. They were arrested a day later and released on October 21.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das Alleges Delhi Airport Stop Before UK Trip

items.summary: In May, a 14-year-old girl named Vaishnavi in the hill hamlet of Peddaporlu developed what is locally called 'chali-jwaram' (chills-fever) after exposure during a storm. Her family initially received only basic treatment at the nearest government Primary Health Centre and declined to travel, as mud roads connecting their village are frequently washed away by torrential rains. After seven days of queuing with blood samples for testing, Vaishnavi was not admitted because the district hospital in Paderu has no overnight facilities; she traveled back and forth three times on a two-wheeler before doctors urged transport to King George Hospital in Visakhapatnam, 106 kilometres away. Her mother said she would prefer taking her daughter to a guru-guniya (local faith healer) who performs animal sacrifices than sending her to the hospital. After spending over Rs 1,000 on fuel across roughly 270 kilometres and around Rs 15,000 for one day's stay at a private hospital in Paderu—while Vaishnavi's family earns about Rs 7,500 per month selling agricultural produce to contractors—she was finally diagnosed with malaria. She later recovered after three days of treatment at the district hospital.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh villages give a reality check to India's 2030 malaria elimination target

items.summary: Maxine Dillion, a 44-year-old self-employed mother of two from Mansfield in Nottinghamshire who earns £32,000 a year, pays £250 a month for five hours' work with Life Laundry after struggling to keep up with her household and personal chores. Launched in 2025 by Alicia Papachristou and Jane Forbes, both based in Wakefield, Yorkshire, the company handles tasks such as arranging insurance, sending school emails, managing online subscriptions, booking handymen, and posting clothing returns on Vinted; much of the work is done remotely, with a monthly visit to Mansfield for jobs requiring physical presence. Life Laundry currently has 25 customers. Amanda Sims Nichols, a business consultant in Austin, Texas who has three children with her attorney husband, pays $2,250 (£1,750) a month for 25 hours of help from Queen of To Do after moving house away from her family support network; she relishes offloading chores such as the weekly food shop and clothes washing. Founded by Kate Ginsberg in 2011, Queen of To Do now has more than 50 active users. Both companies report growing demand as people's lives become increasingly frantic. Ginsberg said some tasks her team handles are very diverse, including flying from Austin to New York City to buy a Christmas gift and finding a new wedding location for a client with just three days' notice due to an incoming hurricane. Jess Baker, a UK chartered psychologist, said using a life PA takes the pressure off keeping hundreds of to-dos in one's head or on lists that might be forgotten, noting otherwise the cognitive load can lead to feelings of being overwhelmed, excess worry and exhaustion. Anna Allington sought help after her husband died; she was 47 when he passed away, and the same week she got leukaemia with a lot to sort out while very unwell. Now 51 and still suffering from cancer's effects because she cannot function executively like before, she pays £1,200 a month for 40 hours of help from Cheshire-based company Vi-Va; her personal assistant helps respond to emails, manage her diary, and make travel plans and bookings. They meet twice a week on Zoom so they can go through all her tasks. Many more women than men use these companies: Queen of To Do says just 20% of its clients are male, while only one of Life Laundry's 25 clients is a man. Forbes suggested some of that disparity reflects mothers still handling the lion's share of household admin in studies, and wondered if some men are too proud to ask for assistance.
items.title: Life admin companies grow as busy parents pay to offload household tasks

items.summary:
The Indian Air Force is expected to take delivery of its first locally manufactured C295 transport aircraft, built jointly by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) and Airbus, with officials reporting the aircraft is undergoing final flight trials and certification as TASL and Airbus target year-end delivery. The plane will join one of the IAF's two existing C295 squadrons based in Agra and Vadodara.

The programme traces to a September 2021 defence ministry contract with Airbus worth ₹21,935 crore for 56 planes aimed at boosting self-reliance in India's defence manufacturing sector. Of the total order, Airbus has delivered 16 aircraft to the IAF in flyaway condition from Spain while the remaining units are being assembled in India; of those remaining, delivery of the first was earlier scheduled for September-end but then-IAF chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh noted in October that minor issues were being resolved. The overall production and delivery programme remains on schedule, with officials stating the remaining 39 aircraft will be delivered by August 2031.

Atmanirbharta (self-reliance) is a key priority for current IAF chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who took over as Chief of the Air Staff on October 31 and outlined his vision using the acronym "VAYU"—V for vigilance and readiness, A for atmanirbharta, Y for yukti (ingenuity), and U for unity of effort. The IAF is expected to begin raising its third C295 squadron next year.

The aircraft will enhance logistics capabilities in forward areas including those near the contested border with China and replace the ageing Avro transport fleet that entered service in the early 1960s. Under the programme, India manufactures more than 13,000 parts and 4,600 sub-assemblies along with all major component assemblies, while Airbus supplies equipment such as engines, landing gear, and avionics; the tactical airlifter is powered by two Pratt & Whitney PW127G turboprop engines. The aircraft can carry up to nine tonnes of payload or 71 personnel or 45 paratroopers at a maximum speed of 480 kmph, operates from short or unprepared airstrips, and has a rear ramp for paradropping troops and cargo.
items.title: IAF to Receive First India-Made C295 Transport Aircraft by December 31

items.summary:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds across parts of South Peninsular India this week, attributing the activity to easterly waves over the Bay of Bengal and off the Kerala-Karnataka coast. Under troughs in these easterlies, IMD says isolated heavy rainfall is very likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal from 23 to 27 November, and over Kerala and Mahe from 24 to 27 November. Fairly widespread to widespread showers are expected across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry from 24 to 26 November; Kerala and Mahe from 24 to 27 November; and Lakshadweep from 25 to 28 November. The agency has also issued warnings for thunderstorms, lightning, and squally weather across the southern peninsula.

While West and Central India are expected to see largely dry weather during the week, IMD reports that minimum temperatures will fall gradually by 3–5°C over Central India until 26 November, by 3–4°C over East India until 27 November, and by 2–3°C over Northwest India until 28 November. Dense morning fog is very likely in isolated pockets of Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura through 25 November, with dense fog also expected over Assam and Meghalaya on 24 and 25 November.

The Met Department cautioned that reduced visibility from the fog could disrupt airport, highway, and railway operations while posing respiratory and eye-irritation risks. In Delhi-NCR, IMD forecasts mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog during morning hours through 26 November, moderate fog likely in a few pockets on 25 and 26 November.

For the national capital specifically, IMD says Tuesday (November 24) will feature mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog in some places during mornings. Daytime maximum temperatures are forecast to hover between 24°C and 26°C—remaining below normal by up to 1.6°C–3.0°C at most places—while minimum temperatures will settle near normal in the 10°C to 12°C range.
items.title: IMD Issues Heavy Rain Alert for Tamil Nadu and Kerala Through November 27

items.summary: Tension and uncertainty prevailed around the Karthigai Deepam lighting at the Tirupparankundram hill shrine in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita limited public assembly and restricted hilltop access. The Supreme Court allowed a restricted one-time lighting of the lamp by authorised officials at 6 PM, barring public access and processions. Following a report identifying the Deepathoon as a British-era survey stone, the state government filed a review petition. Approximately 5,600 police personnel were deployed to manage the situation, while political parties debated the matter and Hindu groups urged adherence to court orders.
items.title: Tension Rises at Tirupparankundram Hill Shrine During Karthigai Deepam Lighting

items.summary: Bihar unit chief of the AIMIM party, Akhtarul Iman, sparked a political controversy with remarks about Muslim bridal traditions. He criticized what he described as the lack of proper veiling during wedding receptions, comparing uncovered brides to courtesans and citing Sharia law's mandate for modesty. His comments were condemned by opposition leaders as sexist and derogatory toward women's dignity. Critics urged party leader Asaduddin Owaisi to respond to the controversy, raising concerns about attitudes toward women's rights and personal freedom.
items.title: AIMIM MLA Akhtarul Iman Draws Criticism Over Comments on Muslim Bridal Practices

items.summary:
On Monday (24 November 2026), UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed delivered remarks in New York on behalf of Secretary-General Antonio Guterres at a special meeting marking the International Day of Solidarity. She said Palestinians in the Gaza Strip are not receiving the safety, assistance or recovery they need despite a ceasefire, describing the devastation as "staggering" with tens of thousands killed and homes, schools and hospitals reduced to rubble while another winter settles in. Mohammed stated there is "no time to waste," "no excuse for inaction," and "no place for impunity," adding that nothing can justify collective punishment against Palestinians and that solidarity must mean acting to end suffering rather than merely bearing witness.

On the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, she said settler violence, demolitions, evictions, land seizures and displacement are driving Palestinian families from their homes at a scale not seen in generations. She warned that Israeli settlement expansion, including efforts to advance the E1 plan, threatens the viability of the two-state solution and called for these activities to stop immediately.

Mohammed also said humanitarian workers must never be targeted and aid must never be obstructed, diverted or used as a bargaining chip. She urged member states to provide political and financial support to UNRWA so it can fulfill its mandate. On recovery, she said rebuilding must be led by Palestinians, go beyond infrastructure reconstruction, and cannot substitute for a political solution; citing a joint UN and World Bank assessment that found the conflict has undone 77 years of human development in Gaza. She concluded that there can be no peace in the Middle East without realizing Palestinian self-determination, calling the two-state solution "the only viable path forward."
items.title: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed Calls for Action on Gaza as Suffering Continues

items.summary: The Trump administration added Megaspeed—the company at the center of the Nvidia scandal—to the Commerce Department's entity list on Monday afternoon, plans first reported by Semafor. The Singapore-based company was placed on the blacklist so that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. According to a filing from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security posted to the Federal Register Monday afternoon, seven total entities were added to the list from Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including various affiliates such as MSFusion, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, and Swiftdata. The filing states that these additions are being made because of "the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users," noting that licenses will be reviewed under a presumption of denial. Technology exports already en route to the targeted companies would still be allowed to go through, per the filing. The addition comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after President Donald Trump implored them to do so; Huang had resigned less than two weeks earlier amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy who was an executive at Megaspeed. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced pressure from others inside the administration—and bipartisan lawmakers—to place Megaspeed on the entity list and explain his decisions around Nvidia, Megaspeed, and chip export controls; tensions became public after news broke of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this month that his agency along with the Pentagon, State Department, and US Trade Representative had backed putting Megaspeed on the entity list "for months" but that "Commerce holds the pen." BIS spokesman Thomas Wackman told Semafor that placing Megaspeed on the Entity List makes it unlawful to export any US-origin goods, software, or technology to the company, including advanced semiconductor chips even if produced outside the United States. The Justice Department is separately investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.
items.title: Commerce Adds Megaspeed to Trade Blacklist Amid Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: At a November 24, 2026 UN Security Council briefing in Istanbul, Russia and Ukraine traded accusations over escalating attacks on Black Sea shipping and energy infrastructure. Moscow's representative accused Ukrainian forces of targeting more than 200 commercial vessels across the Black, Azov, Caspian, Baltic and Mediterranean seas since July, killing or wounding 12 seafarers, while defending its campaign as limited to military-logistical targets and dismissing Western calls for a truce. Russia's envoy also ruled out reviving a grain deal, calling any new agreement 'a scheme of Ukrainian food in exchange for Western weapons,' noting that under the previous arrangement only 3% of exported grain reached countries in need while up to 70% entered EU and Western markets; he said Russia supplies food to 160 countries. Ukraine's representative accused Russia of targeting civilian power grids since mid-July, damaging virtually every power plant alongside more than 800 units of energy equipment, with November barrages shutting down three thermal plants and plunging more than 850,000 people into darkness; he also cited the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant's 28th off-site power loss. On maritime security, Kyiv reported 89 attacks on civilian vessels between June and August, up from 25 in all of 2025, while accusing Russia of looting grain through a 'shadow grain fleet.' The Ukraine Energy Support Fund raised more than €2.4 billion ($2.6 billion) from 41 donors as Kyiv prioritized air defense for winter. US representative urged both sides to immediately halt strikes on energy grids, civilian ports, food distribution sites and commercial shipping, highlighting progress with four pillars aimed at building toward a lasting peace.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Clash at UN Over Black Sea Shipping and Energy Strikes

items.summary: The Airline Pilots' Association of India (ALPA India) has urged the Civil Aviation Ministry to examine whether SpiceJet's financial difficulties are creating risks for flight safety. In a letter dated November 17, signed by Captain Sam Thomas, President and IFALPA Director of ALPA India, the association raised concerns over delayed salary payments to pilots and cabin crew, pending maintenance organisation and spare-parts supplier payments, and employee pressure during repeated flight disruptions. ALPA warned that financial uncertainty and stress from unpaid salaries could affect the alertness, concentration and decision-making of employees responsible for passenger safety, arguing aviation professionals should not perform safety-critical duties while struggling with basic financial commitments. The association also highlighted difficulties faced by pilots, cabin crew and ground staff during delays, cancellations and other operational disruptions, noting frontline employees increasingly face passenger frustration despite having little control over management decisions causing such disruptions. ALPA flagged the possible impact of financial constraints on aircraft maintenance, warning that payment delays to maintenance organisations, spare-parts suppliers and essential service providers could result in grounded aircraft and further operational disruptions while increasing workload pressure on engineering personnel. The association questioned what it described as the DGCA's apparent double standards in enforcing employment-related regulations, pointing out that the regulator strictly applies Civil Aviation Requirements concerning notice periods and No Objection Certificates when pilots want to leave an airline, yet reportedly tells employees the regulator cannot intervene in contractual matters when airlines delay or fail to pay salaries. ALPA argued that if notice periods are justified for flight safety, persistent non-payment of salaries must equally be recognised as a flight safety concern. The association has asked the Civil Aviation Ministry and DGCA to urgently examine the safety implications of financial distress at SpiceJet and other similarly affected airlines, with demands including closer monitoring of aircraft maintenance resources and payments, timely salary payment to pilots and cabin crew, and a faster release and NOC process when employers have demonstrably failed contractual obligations. The letter was marked to the Director General of Civil Aviation and the Prime Minister's Office. These concerns come amid continuing operational difficulties at SpiceJet, with flight disruptions and passenger complaints adding to questions about the airline's financial and operational position.
items.title: ALPA Warns SpiceJet Financial Troubles Raise Flight Safety Concerns

items.summary: Demonstrators gathered in Brussels carrying placards warning that 'Rent is eating into our wages' and 'The rich earn more, the workers pay more,' to oppose approximately €10 billion in proposed spending cuts. The planned savings would affect social security, employment support, and family assistance while burdening low-income earners already strained by high energy costs, inflation, and shrinking purchasing power. Clashes broke out between protesters and riot police as a car burned amid plumes of smoke; officers responded with tear gas, water cannons, and charges, making arrests in the process. The street protests coincided with Prime Minister Bart De Wever's meeting with King Philippe to update him on strained negotiations over Belgium's 2027 budget. Having set a year-end deadline for coalition partners to approve the cuts and warned that the government could collapse if talks fail, De Wever now faces mounting resistance both in parliament and on the streets as he attempts to balance fiscal discipline against demands to protect living standards.
items.title: Belgian Workers March Against Spending Cuts Amid Rising Living Costs

items.summary: Papua New Guinea's parliament is voting to ratify the result of a 2019 referendum in which almost 98% of Bougainvillean voters chose independence. A 'yes' vote would not immediately create an independent nation but would set legal machinery in motion toward self-determination, while a 'no' or deferred vote would trigger further consultations and protective measures.
items.title: PNG Parliament Votes on Ratifying Bougainville Independence

items.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced during a Monday media briefing that India's first bullet train is expected to begin trial runs in May 2027 on the 50-km Surat-Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor. He said electrification work on the section had been completed, while signalling-related work was targeted for completion by January 2027.
items.title: India's First Bullet Train to Begin Trials in May 2027, Railway Minister Announces

items.summary: A Dutch court barred European sales of a BYD vehicle over its resemblance to Jaguar Land Rover's Defender, causing BYD shares to slide Monday and marking a setback for the Chinese automaker's Europe expansion plans. The affected model is not yet on sale in the EU, and Reuters noted it was rare for European automakers to sue over design rights infringement. This case reflects broader efforts by the EU to protect its car industry from Chinese competitors amid aggressive overseas expansion; Chinese brands captured a record 14.5% of Europe's market in September. However, while European automakers may welcome the ruling, the vehicle—nicknamed the 'Temu Range Rover'—has been the UK's best-selling car for months.
items.title: Dutch Court Bars BYD Vehicle Over Range Rover Resemblance

items.summary: Ohio regulators approved construction of an 800-megawatt natural gas plant to power a data center complex in Ashville, Ohio, even though local voters overwhelmingly rejected the project. The permit approval is not unique nationally—energy-hungry developers are building similar gas-fired generation across the U.S.—but critics say it highlights Ohio's leniency toward fossil-fuel projects versus its strict restrictions on solar and wind farms that often face denial due to local opposition.
items.title: Ohio Approves Gas Plant for Data Centers Despite Local Voter Rejection

items.summary: According to findings published in The Innovation, mangrove cover in China more than doubled between 1998 and 2020, while the number of bird species recorded in those areas rose from 148 to 397. This recovery follows decades of steep decline: China lost nearly 70% of its mangroves between 1950 and 1990. Since then, the government has set aside mangrove reserves and restored degraded areas, including former aquaculture ponds, according to researchers who also attribute part of the growth to rising temperatures and increased rainfall favoring mangrove expansion.
items.title: China's Mangrove Cover Doubled and Bird Species Rose From 148 to 397
